2330586.title: Agreement Signed between DBN (Digital Bharat Nidhi) - Department of Telecommunications; Government of Tamil Nadu & TANFINET for Utilisation of BharatNet Network in Tamil Nadu under ABP
2330586.body_html:
Ministry of Communications
Agreement Signed between DBN (Digital Bharat Nidhi) - Department of Telecommunications; Government of Tamil Nadu & TANFINET for Utilisation of BharatNet Network in Tamil Nadu under ABP
Financial Support Approved for Utilisation of BharatNet Network in Tamil Nadu under ABP
Agreement to cover subsidy support for over 5 lakhs rural home fibre connections in Tamil Nadu under ABP and Provide On-Demand Connectivity to 4,767 Villages
Partnership to Strengthen and Connect Rural Telecom Infrastructure across Tamil Nadu
Posted On: 30 OCT 2026 7:07PM by PIB Delhi

In a significant step towards strengthening digital infrastructure and accelerating broadband connectivity across rural Tamil Nadu, Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN) under Department of Telecommunications (DoT) signed a Utilisation Agreement for connecting the rural households under Amended BharatNet Program (ABP) in the State under the State-led model today at Sanchar Bhawan, New Delhi.

The Agreement was signed between Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN), DoT; Government of Tamil Nadu; and Tamil Nadu FibreNet Corporation (TANFINET) for Utilisation of BharatNet Network in Tamil Nadu under ABP.

The Agreement signing ceremony was held in the august presence of Shri Shyamal Misra, Administrator, Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN), Department of Telecommunications. The ceremony was also attended by Shri Atul Anand, Additional Chief Secretary, Artificial intelligence, Information Technology and Digital services department, Government of Tamilnadu (through video conferencing); Shri Papa Sudhakara Rao, Director (Enterprise Business), Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited; Smt. V. Vallidevi, General Manager (Projects), Tamil Nadu FibreNet Corporation and Shri Dinesh Kumar Garg, DDG (ABP Implementation-I), Department of Telecommunications, along with senior officers of DoT, DBN and BSNL.

The Union Cabinet had approved the Amended BharatNet Program on 4th August 2023 with the objective of upgrading, consolidating and expanding the existing BharatNet network to ensure robust and future-ready broadband connectivity to all Gram Panchayats and villages on demand basis.

The Government of India has approved financial subsidy support for utilisation of BharatNet network under Amended BharatNet Program. The initiative is expected to facilitate more than five lakh rural home fibre connections in the state of Tamil Nadu with financial support from the Government of India and significantly enhance delivery of digital services including e-Governance, online education, telemedicine, digital payments and citizen-centric services across rural and remote areas of the State. In addition, 4,767 villages in the state of Tamil Nadu will be provided connectivity on a demand basis to strengthen last-mile connectivity.

The Agreement signed today is expected to accelerate execution of the Program in Tamil Nadu and further advance the vision of a digitally empowered society and knowledge economy.

About Digital Bharat Nidhi

Digital Bharat Nidhi (erstwhile USOF) was established under the Indian Telegraph (Amendment) Act, 2003 w.e.f. 01.04.2002. As per ‘The Telecommunications Act, 2023’ the Universal Service Obligation Fund, has become the Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN). The DBN has mandate to support universal service through promoting access and delivery of telecommunication service in underserved rural, remote and urban areas. It is an attached office of the Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Ministry of Communications.

In order to achieve objectives of DBN, it covers various schemes and projects including BharatNet, 4G Saturation Project, Provision of Mobile Service in uncovered areas of Aspirational Districts, Mobile Services in Left Wing Extremist Areas, Mobile Services in Himalayan and Border areas, Mobile Services in Islands and Mobile Services in North Eastern Areas.

2330568.title: From Economic Challenges To Research Aspirations
2330568.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Economic Challenges To Research Aspirations
 A Success Story Under NFSC Scheme With Financial Assistance of ₹ 24 Lakh
Posted On: 30 OCT 2026 6:56PM by PIB Delhi

The NFSC Scheme reflects the Government of India’s commitment to supporting eligible students in higher education and research, reducing financial barriers and enabling them to work towards their aspirations and contribute to an inclusive, knowledge-driven and developed India.

At 40, Mahendra Kumar (name changed), a resident of Udaipur, Rajasthan, has pursued his academic aspirations with support under the National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students (NFSC) Scheme.

His journey highlights the importance of financial assistance in enabling scholars to overcome economic barriers and work towards academic excellence and national development.

Before receiving support under the scheme, Mahendra faced economic difficulties that created challenges in pursuing his educational goals. Despite these constraints, he remained committed to higher education and aspired to contribute to the country’s development by conducting high-quality research. Financial barriers can make doctoral studies challenging by placing pressure on scholars and limiting their ability to focus fully on research.

For Mahendra, pursuing a Ph.D. was an important step towards advancing his academic goals and contributing to the country’s research and knowledge base. The financial assistance available through the NFSC Scheme offered support to continue his academic journey and address expenses associated with doctoral studies.

Beginning in December 2020, Mahendra received assistance under the NFSC Scheme in the form of fellowship support, House Rent Allowance (HRA) and contingency grants. The total assistance availed by him amounted to ₹ 24 Lakh. This support helped him pursue his Ph.D. and work towards his academic objectives with reduced financial pressure.

 

Mahendra reported that the fellowship fully supported him in pursuing his doctoral studies and academic goals. The assistance helped address economic challenges and enabled him to devote greater attention to his research and academic responsibilities. The combination of fellowship, HRA and contingency support contributed to making his research journey more manageable.

Following the support, Mahendra describes the changes in his academic, professional and personal life as positive. Although he reported no change in income, he considers the overall impact of the fellowship beneficial. The assistance has supported his continued commitment to research and his aspiration to contribute to national development through high-quality academic work.

Mahendra Kumar’s journey demonstrates the role of targeted financial assistance in helping scholars pursue advanced education despite economic challenges.

2330558.title: UPI Acceptance Enabled for Online Bookings at At the Top, Burj Khalifa and Resorts World Sentosa
2330558.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
UPI Acceptance Enabled for Online Bookings at At the Top, Burj Khalifa and Resorts World Sentosa
Indian Visitors to UAE and Singapore Can Now Book Experiences Seamlessly with UPI
Posted On: 30 OCT 2026 6:48PM by PIB Delhi

Indian visitors to the UAE and Singapore can now book experiences seamlessly with UPI. Indian visitors planning travel to two of the world’s premier destinations can now seamlessly book experiences and make online payments using their preferred Unified Payments Interface (UPI) apps. This development marks a significant step in enabling easier, currency-friction-free planning for Indian travellers globally.

NPCI International Payments Limited (NIPL), the international arm of the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), announced its strategic partnerships with the UAE and Singapore on 29th July 2026 and 9th September 2026 respectively, to enable UPI for online bookings. For the UAE, in partnership with NEOPAY and Emaar Entertainment, UPI acceptance is enabled for At the Top, Burj Khalifa, marking the first UAE attraction to implement UPI for e-commerce. For Singapore, in collaboration with FOMO Pay, a leading payment institution, UPI acceptance is expanded to Resorts World Sentosa, a significant step that follows the Singapore market welcoming 1.2 million Indian visitors in 2025.

The integration of UPI for online purchases at world-class global destinations like At the Top, Burj Khalifa and iconic Resorts World Sentosa attractions, including Universal Studios Singapore, the Singapore Oceanarium and Adventure Cove Waterpark, addresses the growing demand for trusted cross-border payment experiences. It strengthens the digital and economic bridge between India and both the UAE and Singapore, empowering Indian travellers with seamless, secure and familiar financial tools.

Key Highlights of the Integration

• Expansion of Digital Horizons: Building on existing partnerships (including QR-based merchant payment network), these new e-commerce milestones extend UPI convenience directly to advanced travel planning for major global attractions. 

• Enhanced Traveler Experience: Millions of digitally-savvy Indian tourists visiting iconic locations can now plan and execute transactions smoothly from India, removing currency friction and making international travel planning and experience simpler. 

• Global Recognition of Digital Payment Infrastructure:These collaboration underlines how India’s indigenous digital payment systems are becoming a critical component of global customer experiences, setting a new benchmark for cross-border financial connectivity.

The Ministry of Finance remains committed to fostering international partnerships that champion digital innovation, streamline cross-border commerce and project India’s technological prowess onto the global stage.

Past Initiative
 · The ticketing facility for the Eiffel Tower via India’s Unified Payments Interface (UPI) was launched on 26th January 2024.

UPI is accepted in ten countries

Singapore, the United Arab Emirates, France, Mauritius, Nepal, Bhutan, Qatar, Sri Lanka, Cambodia and Greece, enabling Indian travellers to make seamless payments abroad through UPI.

Uzbekistan is set to become the 11th on the list, following a commercial agreement announced on 30th August 2026 during the visit of the Hon’ble Prime Minister of India to Uzbekistan.

2330557.title: AIR MARSHAL INDERPAL SINGH WALIA APPOINTED AS THE VICE CHIEF OF THE AIR STAFF
2330557.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
AIR MARSHAL INDERPAL SINGH WALIA APPOINTED AS THE VICE CHIEF OF THE AIR STAFF
Posted On: 30 OCT 2026 6:47PM by PIB Delhi

Air Marshal Inderpal Singh Walia, AVSM VM is appointed as Vice Chief of the Air Staff (VCAS) from 01 November 2026. Presently, he is the Air Officer Commanding-in-Chief of Eastern Air Command.

The Air Officer is an alumnus of the National Defence Academy and was commissioned n the Fighter stream of the Indian Air Force (IAF) on 11 Jun 88. He is qualified on all variants of the MiG-21, MiG-23, MiG-27, Jaguar and Su-30 MKI. In a career spanning almost four decades, the Air Officer has tenanted various command and staff appointments. He has commanded a frontline fighter squadron, the Tactics and Air Combat Development Establishment (TACDE) and was Air Officer Commanding of Air Force Station Bareilly. He has undergone the Advanced Command & Staff Course in the UK and the NDC in Bangladesh. He has headed the Directorate of Air Staff Inspection (DASI) of the IAF, served as the Defence Attache at the Embassy of Japan and South Korea, and was the Senior Air Staff Officer of Eastern Air Command.

He is an avid reader and holds three Post-Graduate degrees in Defence and Strategic Studies. In recognition of distinguished service, he was awarded the Vayu Sena Medal (VM) in 2008 and Ati Vishisht Seva Medal (AVSM) in 2018. He takes over from Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, who will be taking over as the 29th Chief of the Air Staff on 31 October 2026.

2330552.title: Department of Posts Releases Special Commemorative Postage Stamps on Breast Cancer Awareness
2330552.body_html:
Ministry of Communications
Department of Posts Releases Special Commemorative Postage Stamps on Breast Cancer Awareness
Initiative reinforces commitment to early detection, timely treatment and improved health outcomes for women
Posted On: 30 OCT 2026 6:41PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Posts, Ministry of Communications, today released a special souvenir sheet featuring two commemorative postage stamps dedicated to Breast Cancer Awareness at Dak Bhawan, New Delhi. The release was done by Ms. Manisha Sinha, Director General Postal Services, in the presence of Ms. Punya Salila Srivastava, Secretary, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, along with other senior dignitaries and officials from both Ministries. The initiative highlights the role of philately in promoting public awareness and supporting important national health priorities.

Ms. Manisha Sinha, Director General Postal Services, and Ms. Punya Salila Srivastava, Secretary, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, along with other senior officials, jointly release the commemorative postage stamps on Breast Cancer Awareness at Dak Bhawan

Addressing the gathering, Ms. Manisha Sinha emphasised that commemorative postage stamps serve as an important medium to showcase the country's priorities and spread awareness beyond geographical boundaries. She highlighted the importance of regular screening and early detection in combating breast cancer and encouraged families to support women in seeking timely medical advice. She also underscored the potential of postcards as a meaningful medium of connection, encouragement and emotional support for women undergoing treatment.

Ms. Punya Salila Srivastava appreciated the Department of Posts for taking forward the message of women's health through philately. Highlighting the Government's focus on preventive healthcare, she emphasised that regular screening for breast, oral and cervical cancers is an integral part of the national healthcare programme. She also highlighted the importance of strengthening awareness and encouraging women to undergo regular screening for early detection.

Special Commemorative Postage Stamps on Breast Cancer Awareness

Breast cancer is the most common cancer among women in India, with approximately two lakh new cases diagnosed annually. The Government of India has strengthened population-based screening and early detection initiatives under the National Programme for Prevention and Control of Non-Communicable Diseases. Screening services are provided through Ayushman Arogya Mandirs and community health centres, with referral facilities and treatment available through district and tertiary care hospitals.

Separately, the Department of Posts, in collaboration with Fortis Hospital, organised awareness sessions on Breast Cancer and Cervical Cancer, along with interactive sessions on Basic Life Support (BLS) and Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) at Dak Bhawan, promoting preventive healthcare awareness and knowledge of essential life-saving techniques.

The special souvenir sheet is available for sale at Philately Bureaus across India and through the e-Post Office portal.

2330548.title: ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva, Viksit Bharat Quiz’ Sees Participation of Over 7,597 Citizens
2330548.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
‘Nasha Mukt Yuva, Viksit Bharat Quiz’ Sees Participation of Over 7,597 Citizens
Quiz to Remain Open for Participation Until November 25, 2026
Campaign Reaches Over 35.09 Crore People Including 13.99 Crore Youth, 10.91 Crore Women
Over 32. 43 Lakh Activities  Conducted In Educational Institutes, 39.91 Lakh Persons Treated And Rehabilitated; More Than 755 DoSJE Supported De-Addiction Centres Working Across The Country
Over 45.07 Lakh Nasha Mukt Pledges Taken; More Than 02 Lakh Nasha Mukti Mitras Registered As On Date
Posted On: 30 OCT 2026 6:35PM by PIB Delhi

 

 

The online ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva, Viksit Bharat Quiz’ has witnessed participation from over 7,597 citizens as of now, which is increasing rapidly reflecting growing engagement with the initiative.

The quiz was launched on October 26, 2026, by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India.

The Ministry is organising the ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva, Viksit Bharat Quiz’ under the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA) to promote awareness about the harmful effects of substance use and encourage active participation, particularly among young people, in the collective endeavour of building a drug-free India.

The quiz is being conducted from October 26 to November 25, 2026, and is open to all citizens. Participants can access the quiz through the MY Bharat portal.

MY Bharat Quiz QR

Participation Link:
https://mybharat.gov.in/quizzes/yuva/detail/Url9dlIwCinQVSf8lwPB9w/

Launched on August 15, 2020, the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan aims to strengthen drug demand reduction efforts through preventive education, awareness generation, treatment, rehabilitation and community participation. Initially launched in 272 vulnerable districts, the Abhiyaan has since expanded its reach to cover all districts across the country.

Nasha Mukti Mitr Registration QR Code

The campaign has reached over 35.09 Crore people including 13.99 Crore youth and 10.91 Crore women, reflecting the nationwide scale of its awareness and outreach initiatives, as on date.

Under the Campaign, over 32. 43 Lakh activities were conducted in Educational Institutes, 39.91 Lakh Persons have been treated and rehabilitated with more than 755 DoSJE Supported De-addiction Centres working across the country. The total number of Nasha Mukt Pledges taken amount to over 45. 07 Lakh with more than 02 Lakh Nasha Mukti Mitras registered as on date.

 

As the Abhiyaan enters its seventh year, the quiz seeks to deepen public understanding of the harmful effects of substance use, promote informed decision-making and encourage young people to become active ambassadors of awareness and prevention. The initiative reinforces the vision of a Nasha Mukt Bharat and Viksit Bharat, recognising the importance of healthy individuals, families and communities in the country's development.

NMBA Mobile App

The quiz comprises 20 Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs), which participants are required to answer within 10 minutes. A participation certificate is generated for every participant who successfully submits the quiz. Participants can also view the correct answers upon completion, enabling them to enhance their understanding of substance use prevention.

NMBA e-pledge QR Code

Through this digital initiative, the Ministry aims to strengthen community participation, encourage responsible choices and mobilise citizens, especially youth, to contribute to the movement against substance use.

The Ministry encourages all citizens, particularly young people, to participate in the ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva, Viksit Bharat Quiz’ and become active contributors to the collective vision of a drug-free India.

2330549.title: NIFT Makes Significant Achievements under Special Campaign 6, Promoting Cleanliness, Sustainability and Green Campus Initiatives
2330549.body_html:
Ministry of Textiles
NIFT Makes Significant Achievements under Special Campaign 6, Promoting Cleanliness, Sustainability and Green Campus Initiatives
Posted On: 30 OCT 2026 6:34PM by PIB Delhi

The National Institute of Fashion Technology (NIFT),under the Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, has made significant achievements under Special Campaign 6 by undertaking a comprehensive range of cleanliness, sanitation, waste management, infrastructure maintenance and environmental sustainability initiatives across its campus. The campaign was formally inaugurated at the NIFT Delhi campus on 2 October 2026 in the august presence of Secretary, Ministry of Textiles and other senior officers and Directors. The participation of the senior leadership marked the commencement of the campaign and reinforced the Ministry's commitment towards promoting cleanliness, environmental protection and sustainable institutional practices.Conducted from 2 October to 31 October 2026, the campaign aimed to create a cleaner, greener, safer and more sustainable campus environment through active participation of students, faculty and staff.

 

Comprehensive Cleanliness and Improved Campus Hygiene

Extensive cleanliness activities were undertaken across academic blocks, workshops, canteens, hostels, corridors, rooftops, storage areas and other common spaces. Removal of cobwebs, accumulated dust, garbage and unwanted materials, along with cleaning of furniture, fans, computer equipment, water tanks and drainage systems, contributed to improved campus hygiene and sanitation.

Effective Waste Management and Digital Housekeeping

Special emphasis was placed on waste segregation and responsible disposal. E-waste and scrap were taken up for disposal in accordance with prescribed procedures. Disposal of e-files and weeding out of physical records were also undertaken to strengthen digital housekeeping, improve record management and optimise available storage space.

 

Environmental Sustainability and Green Practices

As part of its environmental initiatives, NIFT undertook plantation, horticulture, tree trimming and pruning activities to enhance campus greenery. A demonstration on preparing biodegradable compost using leaves, fruit waste and leftover food items was also organized to promote the productive utilization of organic waste and encourage environmentally responsible practices.

 

‘Craft from Waste’ – Promoting Creativity and Reuse

In an innovative initiative reflecting NIFT's creative and design-oriented ethos, the institute undertook the ‘Craft from Waste’ activity, demonstrating how discarded materials can be transformed into useful and decorative articles. These creatively prepared items were also used to beautify identified campus areas, promoting the principles of reuse, recycling and waste reduction.

 

Infrastructure Maintenance and Campus Beautification

Several maintenance activities were undertaken to improve campus infrastructure, safety and functionality. These included inspection and rectification of electrical installations, repair of defective switches, sockets and hanging wires, maintenance of lifts, hostel buildings, doors,

furniture, fixtures and perimeter fencing. Anti-termite treatment and pest control activities were also carried out across academic, administrative and residential blocks.Further, cleaning and maintenance of heaters, blowers, geysers, HVAC systems, air conditioners, Air Handling Units (AHUs) and air filtration units were undertaken to ensure a clean, hygienic and safe campus environment.

 

Student Participation and Awareness Activities

To encourage awareness and active participation, NIFT organised various competitions and awareness activities during the campaign. These included a slogan-making competition on the theme ‘Importance of Swachhata and E-Waste Management’, along with painting and poem competitions on Swachhata. Posters, banners, placards and standees were also displayed at prominent locations to spread awareness about cleanliness and environmental protection. Winners of the competitions were felicitated to encourage their continued participation.

 

 

Recognition of Housekeeping and Hygiene Personnel

Recognising the valuable contribution of sanitation and housekeeping personnel, NIFT felicitated its housekeeping and hygiene workers on 27 October 2026 for their dedicated efforts in maintaining cleanliness and sanitation across the campus. The initiative acknowledged their important role in maintaining a clean and healthy institutional environment and reinforced the principle of dignity of labour.

Through its dedicated efforts under Special Campaign 6, NIFT has reaffirmed its commitment to the vision of the Ministry of Textiles for promoting cleanliness, environmental sustainability and responsible resource management. The campaign has demonstrated that collective participation, innovative practices and sustained efforts can bring meaningful improvements in institutional cleanliness and environmental protection. These initiatives will further encourage a culture of cleanliness, creativity and sustainability, contributing towards the vision of a cleaner, greener and more sustainable India.

 

***

2330547.title: MCA only performs administrative role in the conduct of appointment process for Judicial and Technical Members of the NCLT
2330547.body_html:
Ministry of Corporate Affairs
MCA only performs administrative role in the conduct of appointment process for Judicial and Technical Members of the NCLT
Posted On: 30 OCT 2026 6:33PM by PIB Delhi

In the light of certain news reports concerning personnel matters relating to the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) made by the Hon’ble Supreme Court, the respective roles of the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) and the NCLT may be seen in the context of the distinct responsibilities assigned to them.

The MCA only performs the administrative role in the conduct of the appointment process for the 63 Judicial and Technical Members of the NCLT.

The NCLT independently undertakes the process for appointment and management of its officers and staff, including Deputy Registrars, Court Officers, Stenographers, Office Assistants and Multi-Tasking Staff. The Government delegated this responsibility to the NCLT vide notification dated 14 October 2019, with a view to ensuring its effective and independent functioning.

2330542.title: ECL pays tribute to Indian Navy with warship model crafted from mining scrap
2330542.body_html:
Ministry of Coal
ECL pays tribute to Indian Navy with warship model crafted from mining scrap
‘Waste to Wealth’ initiative under Special Campaign 6 showcases coal miners’ craftsmanship and commitment to sustainability
Posted On: 30 OCT 2026 6:25PM by PIB Delhi

In a unique gesture of gratitude and respect for the Indian Navy's unwavering commitment to safeguarding the nation's maritime frontiers, Eastern Coalfields Limited (ECL) a subsidiary of Coal India Limited under the Ministry of Coal, on Friday presented a specially crafted model of a warship to the 1 Bengal NCC Naval Unit, Group Headquarters NCC Kolkata ‘C’. Made from discarded components of coal mining machinery, the model symbolises the shared spirit of service, dedication and nation-building that unites coal miners and naval personnel.

The model was meticulously designed and fabricated at ECL's Neamatpur Central Workshop under the ‘Waste to Wealth’ initiative of Special Campaign 6, being implemented across ECL under the guidance of Dr. Satish Jha, Chairman-cum-Managing Director. The creation showcases the technical ingenuity and craftsmanship of ECL's workforce, transforming industrial scrap into a symbol of national pride while promoting resource reutilisation and sustainability.

On behalf of the Chairman-cum-Managing Director, the Functional Directors and the entire ECL Parivar, Maj. S. Tiwari, Chief of Security, ECL, accompanied by Ms. Nishchal Soni, Manager (HR), Neamatpur Central Workshop, presented the model to Commodore Caesar Basu and Commander Sanjib Saran of the Indian Navy as a token of appreciation for the Armed Forces' dedicated service to the nation.

The warship model is among 10 different models created by ECL under the ‘Waste to Wealth’ initiative during the ongoing Special Campaign 6, each conveying a symbolic message on themes of public importance. Developed by creatively repurposing discarded materials, these models highlight the potential of industrial waste as a resource for innovation and meaningful expression.

The initiative reflects ECL's emphasis on innovative waste management, recycling and resource conservation. It also demonstrates how the technical skills and creativity of its workforce can contribute to environmental sustainability while promoting the principles of a circular economy.

The presentation stands as a distinctive expression of appreciation from ECL's coal miners to the Indian Navy, bringing together the values of service, sustainability and national pride. From the depths of coal mines to the vast expanse of the seas, the spirit of serving the nation remains a common bond.

****

Shuhaib. T

2330512.ministry: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
2330512.body_html:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
41st Webinar of the National Good Governance Webinar Series on the theme ‘Sustainability and Replication of the Awarded Initiatives under PMA’ held on 30th October 2026.
Presentations made on Rajkot District initiative, Gujarat by Shri Prabhav Joshi, Joint Managing Director, Gujarat Industrial Development Corporation, Gandhinagar; its Sustainability by Dr. Om Prakash, Collector & District Magistrate, Rajkot; and its replication & expansion by Shri Manish Gurwani, Collector & District Magistrate, Navsari, to national audience.
 
Posted On: 30 OCT 2026 5:45PM by PIB Delhi

The 41st National Good Governance Webinar was held on 30th October 2026 in which the initiative of Rajkot District, awarded the PM’s Award for Excellence in Public Administration, 2024, was presented under the theme ‘Sustainability and Replication of the Initiatives Awarded under PMA’. The presentations included:

(i)       The awarded initiative presented by Shri Prabhav Joshi, Joint Managing Director, Gujarat Industrial Development Corporation (GIDC), Gandhinagar;

(ii)      Sustainability aspects of the initiative presented by Dr. Om Prakash, Collector & District Magistrate, Rajkot;

(iii)     Implementation of the key aspects and further scaling up of the initiative by Shri Manish Gurwani, Collector & District Magistrate, Navsari, Gujarat.

The Webinar was chaired by Shri Puneet Yadav, Additional Secretary, DARPG and was attended by senior officers of the Department. The Webinar was attended from more than 330 locations across India with Senior Officials of Administrative Reforms Departments of States/UTs, District Collectors, State and District field officers, and Officers of Central and State Administrative Training Institutes.

The Prime Minister had directed Department of Administrative Reforms & Public Grievances (DARPG), in April 2022, to hold virtual conferences/ webinars with District Collectors and other officers in which past award winners of PM’s Awards (PMA) for Excellence in Public Administration be invited to present their experiences with the objective of greater dissemination and replication.

Since then, 40 webinars have been held so far. Each webinar is attended by about 1000 officials from Line Departments, State Governments, District Collectors, State Administrative Training Institutes and Central Training Institutes.

2330453.title: DRI deals major blow to Myanmar-linked drug smuggling network; seizes huge consignment of 50 kg methamphetamine tablets and crystal meth in North-East; four arrested
2330453.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
DRI deals major blow to Myanmar-linked drug smuggling network; seizes huge consignment of 50 kg methamphetamine tablets and crystal meth in North-East; four arrested
In another a major intelligence-led operation, DRI uncovers innovative concealment methods involving furniture and tea packets; three vehicles seized
Posted On: 30 OCT 2026 5:00PM by PIB Delhi

In another significant crackdown on cross-border narcotics smuggling in North East, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI), has seized large quantity of 50 kg methamphetamine in the form of tablets (Yaba) and crystal meth, in two back-to-back Intelligence led operations in Mizoram and Assam. The seizures comprise of significantly large quantities of 30 kg methamphetamine tablets and 20 kg crystal methamphetamine. Four persons have been arrested under the relevant provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985.

Acting on specific intelligence inputs regarding the transportation of multiple consignments of narcotic drugs from Zokhawthar towards Aizawl and Silchar, the officers of DRI, with operational assistance from the Assam Rifles intercepted a Mahindra Bolero Camper   on the outskirts of Aizawl along the Aizawl–Champhai Road, on 29th October 2026. A thorough search of the vehicle led to the recovery of 30 brick-sized packets containing pinkish-orange tablets, weighing 30 kg, concealed in a specially constructed cavity inside an office table with a storage cabinet. The use of furniture as cover cargo to camouflage the transportation of narcotics represents a novel modus operandi, apparently intended to make the vehicle appear to be transporting ordinary household or office goods.

On 30th Oct 2026, in another intelligence led operation, the officers of DRI, assisted by the Assam Rifles, intercepted an Ashok Leyland truck and a Bolero Camper at Dholai, approximately 40 km from Silchar. A search of the truck resulted in the recovery of 20 packets crystal methamphetamine, weighing 20 kg.  The packets had been concealed above the driver's cabin and packed in tea packets bearing foreign markings, apparently to evade detection. Field testing indicated the presence of amphetamine in the recovered substance.

In two operations, four persons have been arrested under the NDPS Act, 1985. In addition, all three vehicles used for transporting the contraband have been seized.

Preliminary investigation indicates that the seized drugs were smuggled from Myanmar. The seizure comes in the backdrop of DRI's recent two major seizures of 232 kg and 56 kg of methamphetamine in the North-Eastern region. Together, these successive seizures underscore the scale and persistence of cross-border synthetic drug trafficking as well as DRI's sustained efforts to identify and dismantle the networks facilitating the movement of such drugs from across the international border into the country.  

DRI remains committed to disrupting organised narcotics trafficking networks, preventing the proliferation of synthetic drugs and safeguarding the country from the serious social and public health consequences of drug abuse.

2330429.title: Telecom Regulatory Authority of India
2330429.body_html:
Ministry of Communications
Telecom Regulatory Authority of India
(TRAI) releases draft ‘Guidelines on Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Telecommunication Networks and Provision of Telecommunication Services’ for stakeholders’ comments
Posted On: 30 OCT 2026 4:32PM by PIB Delhi

Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has today released draft ‘Guidelines on Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Telecommunication Networks and Provision of Telecommunication Services’ for stakeholders’ comments.

In February 2026, the Government of India released the ‘India AI Governance Guidelines’ with the goal to harness the transformative potential of artificial intelligence for inclusive development and global competitiveness, while addressing risks it may pose to individuals and society. The guidelines are anchored in seven guiding sutras or principles — Trust is the Foundation, People First, Innovation over Restraint, Fairness & Equity, Accountability, Understandable by Design, and Safety, Resilience & Sustainability.  Part 4 of the guidelines provides practical guidance for industry actors and regulators to increase clarity, predictability and accountability in the ecosystem.

The telecommunication sector constitutes a significant part of India’s digital infrastructure. Today, the telecommunication sector supports connectivity for the public, delivery of public and essential e-services, conduct of trade and commerce, and secure and resilient functioning of the country’s critical information infrastructure. It is critical not only for social, economic and commercial activities but also for national security and emergency response in the country.

At present, AI is increasingly being integrated into telecommunication networks and provision of telecommunication services. With a view to ensuring consistent and responsible implementation of the India AI Governance Guidelines in the telecommunication sector, and to increase clarity, predictability and accountability in the ecosystem, TRAI has decided to frame guidelines on responsible use of AI in telecommunication networks and provision of telecommunication services after following stakeholders’ consultation.
In this regard, a draft of the Guidelines on Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Telecommunication Networks and Provision of Telecommunication Services has been placed on TRAI’s website (www.trai.gov.in) for seeking inputs from stakeholders.  Written comments on the draft guidelines are invited from stakeholders by 27.11.2026

The comments may be sent, preferably in electronic form to Shri Akhilesh Kumar Trivedi, Advisor (Networks, Spectrum & Licensing), TRAI, at advmn@trai.gov.in. For any clarification/ information, Shri Akhilesh Kumar Trivedi, Advisor (Networks, Spectrum & Licensing), TRAI may be contacted at Telephone Number +91-11-20907758.

2330414.title: 24th Instalment of PM-KISAN
2330414.body_html:
PIB Backgrounder
24th Instalment of PM-KISAN
Direct Benefit Transfer of over ₹18,690 crore to 9.34 crore farmers
Posted On: 30 OCT 2026 3:53PM by PIB Delhi

PM-KISAN provides eligible farmer families ₹6,000 annually in three instalments, supporting agricultural investments and household financial stability. The 24th instalment transferred over ₹18,690 crore to 9.34 crore farmers, taking cumulative disbursements beyond ₹4.64 lakh crore. Aadhaar-linked bank accounts, Direct Benefit Transfer, e-KYC and digital verification strengthen transparency and reduce intermediaries. The scheme’s continuation until 2030-31, backed by a ₹3.15 lakh crore financial outlay, reinforces sustained support for farmer income security.

 

PM-KISAN: Strengthening Income Security for Farmers

The government has released the 24th instalment of the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) on 30 October 2026, at Banaskantha, Gujarat. More than 9.34 crore eligible farmers received around ₹18,690 crore in direct financial assistance. The funds were transferred through the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) system, ensuring transparency and eliminating intermediaries. The scheme is widely regarded as a significant initiative towards ensuring ‘Annadata Samman’.

Recently, in July 2026, the Union Cabinet approved continuation of the PM-KISAN Scheme from 2026-27 to 2030-31. A total financial outlay of ₹3.15 lakh crore has been approved for the scheme during this period. The approval reiterates the government’s commitment that the prosperity of farmers forms the foundation of the nation’s prosperity.

Direct Income Support to Small and Marginal Farmers under PM-KISAN

PM-KISAN is a centrally sponsored scheme launched on February 24, 2019. The scheme seeks to provide assured income support to landholding farmer families nationwide with cultivable land. Under the scheme, each eligible farmer family receives annual financial assistance of ₹6,000. This is disbursed in three equal instalments of ₹2,000 into their Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts.

The assistance provided under PM-KISAN has enabled farmers to make timely investments in seeds, fertilizers, irrigation, agricultural machinery and other agricultural requirements. This has enhanced farmers’ productive capacity, reduced their dependence on informal credit and strengthened the financial stability of rural households.

So far, more than ₹4.64 lakh crore has been disbursed to eligible farmer families across the country through 24 instalments. The scheme benefits are provided to farmers after their land records are seeded on the PM-KISAN portal. They also must link their bank accounts to Aadhaar and complete e-KYC verification. Reflecting the government’s continued commitment to strengthening farmers’ income security, the Union Budget 2026-27 has allocated ₹60,000 crore for the PM-KISAN scheme.

The scheme seeks to increase the income of small and marginal farmers by providing financial support for agricultural inputs. This helps in improving crop health and productivity. Providing direct financial assistance also helps reduce farmers’ reliance on informal credit sources and supports the continuity of agricultural activities. PM-KISAN stands out as one of the largest Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) initiatives globally. This underscores its significant institutional mechanism for delivering financial support directly to farmers.

The PM-KISAN Fund Transfer Journey

The process begins with farmer registration through the PM-KISAN portal, mobile app, or Common Service Centres (CSCs). State governments verify eligibility and upload beneficiary details to the portal. The system then validates Aadhaar and bank account details and screens out ineligible applicants. After final state approval, the data is sent to the Public Financial Management System (PFMS) for account verification. Eligible records are used to generate fund transfer requests and payment orders. The Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare issues sanction orders. Payments are then processed through sponsor banks and the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI). Finally, funds are credited directly to farmers’ bank accounts, ensuring fast, transparent, and efficient delivery of benefits.

Targeting, Beneficiary Identification, and Database Management

State Governments are responsible for identifying eligible farmer households and developing a comprehensive beneficiary database. This database includes key details such as name, age, category, Aadhaar number, bank account information, and mobile number. States ensure the accuracy of these records to prevent duplicate payments. These records are regularly updated, digitized, and linked to Aadhaar and bank account information to enable seamless DBT of benefits.

The lists of eligible beneficiaries are publicly displayed at the village level to promote transparency. This also enables farmers, who may have been inadvertently excluded, to seek inclusion through the appropriate grievance redressal mechanisms. Additionally, States and UTs conduct recovery proceedings for the benefits that have been disbursed to ineligible individuals. These include income tax payers, government employees, public sector undertaking (PSU) personnel, and holders of constitutional posts. As of December 2025, a total amount of ₹416.75 crore has been recovered from ineligible beneficiaries nationwide.

Multi-Tier Monitoring and Grievance Redressal Framework

Monitoring of the PM-KISAN is undertaken through a multi-tiered institutional framework operating at the national, state, and district levels. At the national level, the review mechanism is chaired by the Cabinet Secretary. State and District Monitoring Committees supervise implementation within their respective jurisdictions.

Farmers can register grievances through the PM-KISAN portal and the Centralized Public Grievance Redressal and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS). This facilitates timely resolution and transparent grievance management. During FY 2024–25, a total of 24,605 grievances were recorded on the PM-KISAN portal.

Technology-Enabled Service Delivery System under PM-KISAN

PM-KISAN is supported by a farmer-centric digital infrastructure that streamlines access and enhances transparency in the delivery of benefits. Aadhaar-based authentication forms a key pillar of the system, facilitating secure beneficiary identification and payment verification. Farmers can complete e-KYC using:

  • OTP-based authentication
  • Biometric authentication
  • Face authentication

The PM-KISAN web portal serves as the central digital platform for beneficiary registration, verification, and data management. It maintains a unified national database of farmers and facilitates fund transfers through integration with the Public Financial Management System (PFMS). It also enables real-time monitoring of financial transactions nationwide. The portal further provides location-wise lists of beneficiary farmers, thereby enhancing transparency in programme implementation.

Complementing the portal, the PM-KISAN mobile application, launched in 2020, extends these services to mobile users. The application enables farmers to undertake self-registration, track the status of benefit transfers, and complete e-KYC verification. In 2023, the application was upgraded with a Face Authentication feature. This allows farmers to complete e-KYC by scanning their faces, thereby eliminating the need for OTP or fingerprint-based verification. Hence, this measure has been proven instrumental in improving accessibility of this scheme.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) Support System: Kisan-eMitra

In September 2023, the Government introduced Kisan-eMitra, an AI-enabled chatbot integrated with the PM-KISAN digital ecosystem. It was developed with technical support from the EkStep Foundation and BHASHINI. The chatbot provides farmers with real-time information on payments, registrations, and eligibility under the scheme in multiple Indian languages.

The platform offers 24/7 assistance in 11 major languages: Hindi, English, Tamil, Bengali, Odia, Malayalam, Gujarati, Punjabi, Telugu, Marathi, and Kannada. Hence, this improves accessibility for a diverse user base. Through voice- and text-based queries, farmers can check the status of their applications, track payment updates, and obtain scheme-related information.

Building Agricultural Resilience through Sustained Income Support

PM-KISAN has emerged as a key pillar of farmers’ income security through timely, direct financial assistance. The disbursement of the 24th instalment reinforces this commitment, reaching over 9.34 crore farmers with ₹18,690 crore. With cumulative disbursements exceeding ₹4.64 lakh crore, the scheme continues to support agricultural investments and rural household stability. Its technology-enabled delivery system promotes transparency, accountability, and wider access. The approved continuation until 2030-31 further underscores the long-term commitment to farmer welfare. By strengthening farmers’ capacity to invest in agricultural inputs and sustain farming activities, PM-KISAN advances a broader vision of inclusive agricultural development and prosperity for India’s farming community.

2330411.title: English rendering of PM's speech at the launch of development projects in Banaskantha, Gujarat
2330411.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
English rendering of PM's speech at the launch of development projects in Banaskantha, Gujarat
Posted On: 30 OCT 2026 3:51PM by PIB Delhi

Bharat Mata Ki Jai.

Bharat Mata Ki Jai.

Popular Chief Minister of Gujarat Shri Bhupendra Bhai Patel, Deputy Chief Minister Bhai Harsh Sanghvi ji, Speaker of the Legislative Assembly Shri Shankarbhai Chaudhary, all ministers of the Gujarat Government, Members of Parliament and Members of the Legislative Assembly, other public representatives, brothers and sisters.

Today, through technology, farmers from every district of the country are connected with us. Today, through technology, farmers from every village of Gujarat are connected with us. Chief Ministers of different states, ministers, all of them are with us today in this important programme for farmers. I heartily welcome all of them as well.

Today, Banaskantha has established its stature. Just now, I was watching on the screen that perhaps such a large gathering seated on charpoys has never been held anywhere in the world. For the people of the country too, it must be an amazing sight that everyone in this gathering is seated on charpoys. Today, Banaskantha has revived this great tradition of our villages. Had you informed the Guinness Book of World Records in advance, they would certainly have recorded it as a world record. It was just mentioned here a moment ago.

The responsibility that you entrusted to me has now completed twenty-five years. And look at the coincidence, after completing twenty-five years, my first visit has been to our Banaskantha. Let me remind you that after becoming Chief Minister in 2001, my first major public programme as Chief Minister was held in Deesa. The older people here will remember that Lok Kalyan Mela. That programme was perhaps historic. Three lakh people from a single district attended it. I do not believe that record has been broken to this day. That record belongs to Banaskantha. The journey began there, and today I have got the opportunity to present an account of twenty-five years of service at the same place.

Only a few days after Navratri, I have received the opportunity to come to the sacred land of Mother Amba. I bow at the feet of Mother Amba. A short while ago, projects dedicated to women, children, farmers, and livestock rearers were inaugurated and foundation stones laid here. A new instalment of PM-Kisan Samman Nidhi has also reached the accounts of crores of small farmers across the country. I extend my heartfelt congratulations to the people of Gujarat, to the people of the country, and to farmers across India.

Friends,

The people of Gujarat and Banaskantha should forgive me, but I have to speak in Hindi today because people from all over the country are connected with this programme. You permit me to speak in Hindi, don't you? Very good.

Friends,

Our farmers, our food providers, are among the strongest pillars of a Developed India. Our government has always prioritised the welfare and empowerment of farmers. Compared to 2013–14, the agricultural budget of the country has now increased more than five times. PM-Kisan Samman Nidhi has become a part of the lives of crores of small farmers. Today, more than ₹18,000 crore has been transferred into the accounts of nearly ten crore farmers. More than fifty lakh farmers of Gujarat have also benefited from it. More than ₹1,000 crore has been deposited into their accounts. In Banaskantha alone, nearly ₹50 crore has reached the accounts of lakhs of farming families.

Friends,

Because of our government's policies over the past years, farmers have received benefits or savings worth more than ₹50 lakh crore. Fifty lakh crore rupees. Let me give you an example of just five schemes. Around ₹4.5 lakh crore under PM-Kisan Samman Nidhi has directly reached the bank accounts of small farmers. Sister, you have defeated me. I thought you would sit down after a while because your hands would start hurting. I request the SPG personnel to collect that beautiful picture which this daughter has brought. Otherwise, she will grow tired holding it up. They will collect it from here, my child. Please stay where you are. Let the SPG personnel collect it. After Independence, the needs of small farmers were never truly understood. Nobody paid attention to them. Yet small farmers account for more than 85 percent of all farmers in our country. More than 85 percent. It is our government that understood their concerns and supported them through PM-Kisan Samman Nidhi.

Friends,

Over the past few years, global uncertainties caused fertiliser prices to surge sharply. But a government dedicated to farmers did not allow that burden to fall upon them. The government spent nearly ₹16 lakh crore on this. To ensure that fertilisers remain affordable for you, we had to spend ₹16 lakh crore from the national treasury, so that the burden would not fall upon our farmers.

Friends,

Previous governments repeatedly misled farmers on Minimum Support Price. But ours is the government that fulfilled its MSP promise. Over the past twelve years, farmers growing wheat and paddy have received ₹24 lakh crore in MSP payments directly into their accounts.

Friends,

Our government has provided farmers with a powerful safety net through the PM Fasal Bima Yojana. We launched crop insurance on a large scale. During the past ten to twelve years, farmers have received more than ₹2 lakh crore in crop insurance compensation. Whenever crops suffered losses, over ₹2 lakh crore reached farmers through insurance support. We are continuously trying to reduce farmers' irrigation costs as well. PM-KUSUM is playing an increasingly significant role in this effort. Under this scheme, nearly twelve lakh solar pumps have already been provided. Twelve lakh pumps powered by solar energy have been given to farmers for irrigation. Because of this, the need for electricity and diesel has reduced substantially. If these solar pumps had not been provided, farmers would have had to purchase more than 80 crore litres of diesel. That entire expense has been saved by lakhs of farmers. And besides that, additional electricity has also been generated. If viewed in one way, these five schemes and decisions alone have either directly benefited farmers or saved them the equivalent of ₹50 lakh crore. This is an enormous figure. These ₹50 lakh crore have increased farmers’ incomes and strengthened Indian agriculture.

Friends,

Agriculture is our tradition. Agriculture is our culture. Agriculture is our culture. During the past twelve years, our government has extensively integrated science and technology into farming. We have linked agriculture and animal husbandry with scientific methods. Soil Health Cards are an excellent example of this. Earlier, farmers found it difficult to determine what type of fertilizer their fields required and in what quantity. Soil Health Cards solved this problem. Today, more than 26 crore Soil Health Cards are in the hands of farmers. These have modernised farming practices.

Friends,

Changing weather patterns are a major challenge for farmers. Therefore, our effort is to continuously provide farmers with new seed varieties that are better suited to changing climatic conditions. Over the past years, around three thousand new seed varieties have been made available to farmers.

Friends,

Animal husbandry is an important part of our rural economy, and our sisters have a major role in it. During the past decade, we have strongly promoted the use of science and technology in animal husbandry and the dairy sector. When livestock breeds improve, milk production increases. As Shankarbhai was saying earlier, we want one cow to produce as much milk as four cows once did. If animals receive timely vaccination and treatment, losses due to disease are reduced. In other words, healthier animals mean higher incomes for our livestock-rearing brothers and sisters.

Friends,

You are all familiar with the National Gokul Mission. Through it, indigenous breeds are being preserved and scientific breeding is being promoted. The new research centre established in Banaskantha will further strengthen this mission. Indigenous cattle breeds such as Gir, Sahiwal, and Kankrej, and buffalo breeds such as Mehsana, Murrah, and Jaffarabadi, will be preserved here. At the same time, major work will be done to improve their quality. For the Kankrej breed, this is the first facility of its kind in the country. Consider a farmer who owns a high-quality cow that produces more milk and remains healthy at a lower cost. Naturally, that farmer would want future generations of that cow to retain those same qualities. Modern technologies such as IVF help achieve exactly that. They increase the likelihood that superior traits will pass on to future generations. The direct benefit of this goes to livestock rearers.

Friends,

Protecting livestock from disease is also one of our priorities. Foot-and-mouth disease affects both animal health and milk production. Therefore, we launched a nationwide free vaccination campaign. So far, nearly 150 crore vaccine doses have been administered to animals. The livestock of more than eight crore farmers have received free vaccinations. This has also reduced the financial burden on livestock rearers.

Friends,

The impact of these efforts is visible in milk production as well. In 2013–14, a cow or buffalo produced on average less than five litres of milk per day. This was the situation when you sent me to Delhi. Less than five litres a day. Today, the national average has increased to around eight litres per day. India’s growth rate in milk productivity is the fastest in the world. India ranks number one globally in milk production. The benefits have reached villages, and the incomes of farming families have increased.

Friends,

We want livestock rearers to earn not only from milk but also from dung. Infrastructure is being developed for producing biogas, bio-CNG, and organic fertilisers from dung and agricultural residues. Institutions like Banas Dairy have an important role in this. Today, foundation stones have also been laid for two bio-CNG plants. Our objective is clear: healthier livestock, higher milk production, and complete utilisation of dung. We are transforming animal husbandry into not merely a tradition but also a strong means of increasing farmers’ incomes and enriching villages. I was interacting with the women here earlier. They told me they supply milk worth ₹2 crore. Milk worth ₹2 crore. Then I asked them how much education they had received. They replied, “Four books,” and yet they supply milk worth ₹2 crore.

Friends,

Over the past years, we have worked with a holistic approach for the prosperity of villages. Just look at the fisheries sector and see how much it has expanded. You will be pleased to know that India’s seafood exports have more than doubled. Our fishermen go out to sea, catch fish and shrimp, and sell them. Today, this sector has made enormous progress, and demand across the world has risen sharply. Cooperation in the fisheries sector is also being promoted.

Friends,

There is another sector that has provided an additional source of income for our farmers. That sector is beekeeping. Over the past twelve years, honey production has doubled. I remember that when I came to Banaskantha, I urged all of you to bring about a Sweet Revolution, a Honey Revolution. Today Banaskantha is setting new records in honey production. When I was interacting with the women earlier, they told me they sell honey worth ₹35 lakh. You will be proud to know that India has become the world's second-largest exporter of natural honey. In this Sweet Revolution, the contribution of our women’s self-help groups is also steadily increasing.

Friends,

A few days ago, on 7th October, I completed twenty-five years as head of government. It feels as though it happened only yesterday. Yes, it feels like yesterday itself, when I first took the oath on 7th October 2001. You all gave your Narendra Bhai immense affection and immense love.Today, I felt a little awkward here. Whatever is said in the rest of the country is one thing, but here Shankarbhai said, “Prime Minister Sahib, Prime Minister Sahib.” Tell me honestly, how will such an address go down my throat? Here, people habitually say, “Our Narendra Bhai has come.” Doesn't it feel better to say that? What joy is there in saying “Prime Minister Sahib”? And when my brothers from Gujarat say “Our Narendra Bhai,” my heart overflows with emotion. More than affection, every Gujarati taught me something. They guided me towards the right path and inspired me. At that time, I knew nothing about government offices, government functioning, or files. A person from an ordinary family, whose generations had never even dreamed of becoming the head of a village, was entrusted by you with the responsibility of serving first Gujarat and then the nation. Earlier while speaking with the women, they asked me how ideas such as Jyotigram, bringing water, natural farming, and initiatives for livestock came to me. I told them that there was no special formula. You taught me everything, and I simply went and implemented it.

Friends,

I have always known only two things: service to the people is service to the nation, and the development of Gujarat leads to the development of India. Everything else, how to work and how to move forward, you taught me. Whatever I have been able to do for the nation belongs to all the citizens of India, and to all of you as well. For this, I will remain indebted to you for my entire life. Until my final breath, I will remain devoted to service. Service, service, and service to the people of the country and to all of you.

Friends,

The senior citizens present here will still remember the old days. Twenty-five years ago, when I used to come here, there were severe problems of electricity and water. Even then, I used to say that we must save electricity and water. Farmers would protest against me, saying, “Who is Modi to tell us to save water? He won't even give us electricity.” I kept arguing with you, and eventually you accepted what I was saying. And today, just look at where we have come from and where we have reached. Those old problems now remain only in memories. Today, I will once again tell you the same thing: we must save water, and we must save electricity as well.

Friends,

The waters of the Narmada and modern technologies such as drip irrigation have transformed Banaskantha. They have changed both the face and the destiny of Banaskantha. Banaskantha’s potatoes are now world-famous. No one can come to a person from Banaskantha and say, “I will turn potatoes into gold,” because he will reply, “I am already doing that.” We have a cooperative brand like Banas Dairy here, which is expanding the cooperative movement to other parts of the country, including Kashi. I am especially grateful to Banas Dairy because even in my Kashi, people are benefiting from your experience and your service. Now, even the French fries potato processing plant has expanded its capacity. This will make it possible to purchase a larger quantity of potatoes. This is a major facility and support for potato farmers.

Friends,

A Cluster Development Programme is being implemented for farmers engaged in fruit and vegetable cultivation. Under this programme, twelve clusters have been approved today. These clusters are associated with fruits and vegetables such as tomatoes, potatoes, chillies, grapes, bananas, onions, oranges, pomegranates, and cocoa. Under this initiative, farmers will be supported in establishing new orchards and rejuvenating old ones. People will be trained and guided for the rejuvenation of older orchards, and subsidies will be provided for the entire project. The two clusters approved in North Gujarat will greatly benefit potato farmers of Banaskantha and Sabarkantha.

Friends,

Today, several other development projects related to Gujarat have also been inaugurated and launched. Gujarat has received two new railway services: the Ahmedabad–Varanasi Sabarmati Express and the Mehsana–Becharaji–Sabarmati MEMU train. Both are highly significant rail connectivity projects. In addition, the Ahmedabad Metro service is also being expanded. Today, the foundation stone has been laid for metro projects connecting GIFT City and the airport. The Ahmedabad–Mehsana Highway is now set to be expanded from four lanes to eight lanes.

Friends,

Today, more than 4,000 modern Anganwadis are also being inaugurated for the children of Gujarat. Nearly four lakh children and pregnant mothers will benefit from them.

Friends,

Every such effort is aimed at making India a developed nation. Today, every farmer, every young person, and every daughter and sister in the country is moving forward with the resolve of building a Developed India. But unfortunately, some people do not like this. Some people are unable to accept it. These are people who want to see the country in difficulty. They derive satisfaction from seeing the nation in trouble. Whenever challenges arise for the country, they feel happy.

Friends,

A recent example of this is the war taking place around Iran and the Gulf region. At a time when India is united in dealing with its consequences, these people were busy spreading rumours. Rumours were spread among farmers that fertilisers would not be available. Artificial queues were created and the atmosphere was disturbed. Women were frightened by being told that cooking gas would no longer be available, asking them how they would cook food and how their children would go to school. Their plan was to create panic and disorder in the country so that they could defame Modi.

Friends,

I want to remind the farmer brothers and sisters of this country that I had said Modi would stand firmly with you. And you can see that even though the war is still continuing, Modi did not allow any shortage of fertilisers for farmers. We did not allow fertiliser supplies to run short.

Friends,

Because of this war, fertiliser prices around the world have risen sharply. The chemicals used in producing fertilisers have also become much more expensive. Yet the government did not allow this burden to fall on farmers. A bag of urea that costs around ₹3,000 elsewhere in the world is available to Indian farmers for less than ₹300. The global price of a bag of urea is around ₹3,000, but the government bears that burden and provides it to you for around ₹300. The price of a bag of DAP fertiliser has crossed ₹5,000 globally. But Indian farmers receive the same bag for around ₹1,350. The nation is providing this support so that our farmers become stronger and their lives improve.

Friends,

In a world full of uncertainty, India’s rapid development has become a new source of hope for the entire world. In such a situation, we must continue moving forward on the path of Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat - One India, Great India. And tomorrow, the 31st of October, is a day to strengthen this resolve. Tomorrow is the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and National Unity Day. The entire nation will celebrate National Unity Day. On this day, the Run for Unity is organised across the country. Reports are coming in from all directions about the grand preparations being made for the Run for Unity. I would especially urge all citizens of the country, particularly our young friends, to participate enthusiastically in the Run for Unity tomorrow morning.

Friends,

Every year, the Unity Festival is celebrated in Ekta Nagar on the morning of 31st October. But this year, keeping the Run for Unity and other programmes in mind, it will be held in the evening instead of the morning. This is a change from previous years. Tomorrow at 5:30 in the evening, a grand Unity Festival will be celebrated in Ekta Nagar. The programme will be organised on a very large scale. You should watch it on television. There will be such a parade on the soil of Gujarat that it will remind you of the Republic Day celebrations in Delhi. Do watch it. There will be parades by police and security forces, and impressive tableaux will be displayed. I urge all citizens of the country to join this programme tomorrow evening as well. From Kashmir to Kanyakumari, from Kutch to Kamakhya, the entire nation should pay tribute to Sardar Patel and reaffirm the resolve of Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat. With this appeal, I once again extend my best wishes to all of you for these development works.

Thank you very much.

The sisters seated at the back are offering their blessings to me. Mothers, I bow at your feet. Your blessings give me tremendous strength. I am deeply grateful to all of you.

Bharat Mata Ki Jai!

Bharat Mata Ki Jai!

Disclaimer: This is an approximate English translation of the Prime Minister’s address. The original address was delivered in Hindi, with some portions in Gujarati, which have been translated to convey their intended meaning.

2330384.title: TRAI released findings of Independent Drive Test (IDT) conducted across Adoni - Mantralayam and Hyderabad nearby areas, during the month of September 2026
2330384.body_html:
Ministry of Communications
TRAI released findings of Independent Drive Test (IDT) conducted across Adoni - Mantralayam and Hyderabad nearby areas, during the month of September 2026
Posted On: 30 OCT 2026 3:04PM by PIB Delhi

The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has released findings of Independent Drive Test (IDT) conducted across Adoni - Mantralayam and Hyderabad nearby areas , during the month of September 2026, for information of general telecom consumers. The purpose of this drive test is to assess and verify real time quality of mobile network services (both voice & data) provided by Telecom Service Providers (TSPs). During the IDT, TRAI captures performance of TSPs for key Quality of Service (QoS) parameters like Coverage, Call Drop Rate (CDR), Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), data Download (DL) and Upload (UL) throughput etc., which are then published to inform Consumers and encourage TSPs to improve their services.

These IDTs have been designed to capture on ground mobile network performance of all TSPs across diverse usages environment like cities, hotspots, public transport hubs, etc. In this type of drive testing, live data and voice sessions are established using SIM cards from all TSPs over 2G, 3G, 4G, and 5G networks. Multiple advanced test handsets are used, and the sessions are monitored and analysed in real-time using advanced Software Systems.

TRAI, through its appointed agency, conducted drive tests across City drive – 1. Hyderabad 63 Kms, Hotspot locations –2 and walk test 21.5Km, during 15th-16th September 2026 in AP LSA. 2.Kurnool District Adoni-Mantralayam and nearby areas 201.8Kms, Hotspot locations – 6, during 17th-18th September 2026 in AP LSA. These tests were conducted under the supervision of the TRAI Regional Office Hyderabad. The observations presented in drive test reports represent the performance of the TSPs on the area/ route under test on the day/ time of conducting the drive test.

Drive Test Route Map: The following map provides overview of drive test routes indicating City drive, Inter-operator calling and Hotspots, as per the legends shown on the map: -

Key Parameters Assessed

  1. Coverage Gap: Percentage of samples, for which signal strength observed less than the minimum prescribed signal strength for respective technology (2G/ 3G/ 4G/ 5G).
  2. Voice Services: Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), Drop Call Rate (DCR), Call Setup Time, Call Silence Rate, Speech Quality (MOS).
  3. Call Silence Instance: Number of call silence instance occurred during the calls.
  4. Data Servies: Download/ Upload Throughput, Latency, Jitter, Packet Drop Rate

The overall mobile network performance in Balasore City for the key parameters has been summarised below: -

The overall mobile network performance across Hyderabad city and nearby areas (Andhra Pradesh LSA)

a)   Coverage Gap - The signal strength observed during voice testing on the drive test route in auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having poor signal strength out of the total samples collected, was 321/8478 for Airtel, 2014/7767 for BSNL, 1439/7740 for RJIL and 1139/8287 for VIL. Details of the coverage gaps have been provided in the map Annexed.

The signal strength observed during voice testing on the drive test route in auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having Limited service out of the total samples collected, was 0/8478 for Airtel, 0/7767 for BSNL, 0/7740 for RJIL and 0/8287 for VIL. Details of the coverage gaps have been provided in the map Annexed.

b)    Dropped Calls - Dropped calls, measured as the number of dropped calls out of the number of successfully established calls, were 0/74 for Airtel, 4/72 for BSNL, 1/74 for RJIL and 0/71 for VIL. Details of the dropped call locations have been provided in the map Annexed.

c)    Call Silence Instance - Call silence instances, measured as the total number of silence instances observed for > 3 seconds out of the total calls established, were 0/69 for Airtel, 0/58 for BSNL 6/67 RJIL and 6/69 for VIL. Details of the call silence instance locations have been provided in the map Annexed.

d)    Out of the total calls established, the number of calls with a poor speech quality score (Mean Opinion Score below 3) were 19/441 for Airtel, 201/326 for BSNL, 66/453 for RJIL and 44/460 for VIL.

e)    Data Download and Upload Throughput:

i)  Data Download performance (Overall): Average download speed was observed as 82.88 Mbps for Airtel (5G/4G), 7.13 Mbps for BSNL (3G), 145.79 Mbps for RJIL (5G/4G) and 41.41 Mbps for VIL (5G/4G/2G). Detail of Download throughput has been provided in the map Annexed.

ii) Data Upload performance (Overall): Average upload speed was observed as 14.75 Mbps for Airtel (5G/4G), 4.35 Mbps for BSNL (3G), 11.40 Mbps for RJIL (5G/4G) and 12.83 Mbps for VIL (5G/4G/2G). Detail of Upload throughput has been provided in the map Annexed

The overall mobile network performance across Adoni-Mantralayam and nearby areas (Andhra Pradesh LSA)

  1. Coverage Gap - The signal strength observed during voice testing on the drive test route in auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having poor signal strength out of the total samples collected, was 1323/37685 for Airtel, 8339/35351 for BSNL, 633/36991 for RJIL and 4155/37273 for VIL. Details of the coverage gaps have been provided in the map Annexed.

The signal strength observed during voice testing on the drive test route in auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having Limited service out of the total samples collected, was 0/37685 for Airtel, 140/35351 for BSNL, 0/36991 for RJIL and 6/37273 for VIL. Details of the coverage gaps have been provided in the map Annexed.

b)    Dropped Calls - Dropped calls, measured as the number of dropped calls out of the number of successfully established calls, were 0/331 for Airtel, 15/317 for BSNL, 0/330 for RJIL and 6/310 for VIL. Details of the dropped call locations have been provided in the map Annexed.

c)    Call Silence Instance - Call silence instances, measured as the total number of silence instances observed for > 3 seconds out of the total calls established, were 12/313 for Airtel, 29/291 for BSNL 2/314 RJIL and 11/307 for VIL. Details of the call silence instance locations have been provided in the map Annexed.

d)   Out of the total calls established, the number of calls with a poor speech quality score (Mean Opinion Score below 3) were 83/2431 for Airtel, 1022/1993 for BSNL, 157/2630 for RJIL and 150/2564 for VIL.

e)    Data Download and Upload Throughput:

i)  Data Download performance (Overall): Average download speed was observed as 118.55 Mbps for Airtel (5G/4G), 10.19 Mbps for BSNL (3G), 209.11 Mbps for RJIL (5G/4G) and 12.27 Mbps for VIL (5G/4G/2G). Detail of Download throughput has been provided in the map Annexed.

ii) Data Upload performance (Overall): Average upload speed was observed as 18.73 Mbps for Airtel (5G/4G), 6.05 Mbps for BSNL (3G), 14.20 Mbps for RJIL (5G/4G) and 5.37 Mbps for VIL (5G/4G/2G). Detail of Upload throughput has been provided in the map Annexed.

Locations of Dropped Calls and Call Silence instances can be seen by clicking red dot on the map Annexed.

Details of drive test route and area covered during the IDT is as under:-

City:

Hyderabad - Khajaguda, Narsingi, Attapur, Anergia, Pashambanda, Shamshabad, Gollapalle Khurd, Manchirevula and Vishal Sanjivini etc.

Adoni - Mantralayam and nearby area-Basaladoddi, Chinnatumbalam, Kup Gal, Ballekallu, Pandavagallu, Adoni, yemminganur, Halaharvi, Mantralayam, Rachumarri, Sunkeswari, Budur, Nandavaram and Chinnakottaliki etc.

Walk Test- 1. AIG Hospital Gachibowli Hyderabad 2. My Home Raka-Hafeezpet-Hyderabad 3. Rajiv Gandhi International Airport Hyderabad 4. Sri Raghavendra Swamy Matha Mantralayam

Hotspot - The hot spot locations, capturing stationary user experience are 1. Adoni Arts and Science College 2. Area Hospital Yemmiganur 3. General Post Office Koti Hyderabad 4. Mantralayam Bus Stand 5. Mantralayam Road Railway Station 6. Rajiv Gandhi International Airport Hyderabad 7. Senior Civil Court Adoni 8. Sri Raghavendra Swamy Matha Mantralayam

The findings of this IDT report have been shared with respective TSPs for taking further necessary action at their end. Detailed reports of IDT are made available on the TRAI website at www.trai.gov.in. For any clarification or additional information, an email can be sent to adv.hydreabad@trai.gov.in or Regional Office of TRAI can be contacted on telephone no.  040-23000761.
