2328543.body_html:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways Strengthens Swachhata Drives and Promotes Good Governance under Special Campaign 6
Posted On: 26 OCT 2026 5:07PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW) and its organisations are actively implementing Special Campaign 6, making significant progress towards achieving the identified targets. The campaign focuses on key areas, including the disposal of e-waste and scrap, effective records management, space optimisation and expeditious grievance redressal, in alignment with the Government of India’s vision of Swachhata, digital transformation and good governance.

As part of the ongoing campaign, 173 cleanliness Campaigns have been conducted, 33,199 physical and e-files have been reviewed out of which 9,808 files have been closed/weeded out. Revenue worth Rs. 9.79 crores has been generated from scrap/ e-waste disposal and 88,171 sq. ft. of space has been freed, leading to improvement in office space management and environment friendly workspace and surroundings.

Among the notable best practices undertaken during Special Campaign 6 is the transformation of Kumartuli Ghat by Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port, Kolkata (SMPK), in collaboration with Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Ltd. (APSEZ). The initiative aims to transform the ghat, which had fallen into a dilapidated condition due to prolonged neglect, into an inclusive, clean and sustainable public space, demonstrating the campaign’s emphasis on the rejuvenation of public spaces and community welfare.


Senior officers of the Ministry have actively participated in Swachhata-related activities, setting an example through their direct involvement in cleanliness drives, beautification of office premises and improvement of surrounding areas. The participation of officers and staff has reinforced the importance of cleanliness, workplace discipline and collective responsibility in institutionalizing Swachhata across the Ministry and its organisations.

2328513.title: From Addiction To Independence Karimganj Assam’s Rahul Sharma’s Journey Of Recovery And Rehabilitation
2328513.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Addiction To Independence Karimganj Assam’s Rahul Sharma’s Journey Of Recovery And Rehabilitation
NAPDDR Supports Recovery, Livelihood Restoration and Social Reintegration Through Comprehensive De-addiction Services
Posted On: 26 OCT 2026 4:41PM by PIB Delhi

The National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR) under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, continues to focus on the  prevention, treatment and rehabilitation of individuals affected by the substance dependence.

The journey of Rahul Sharma (name changed), a 30-year-old resident of Jalalnagar village in Karimganj district, Assam, highlights how timely intervention, compassionate care and comprehensive rehabilitation can help individuals overcome challenges and work towards a healthier and more independent life.

Following the death of his father, Rahul had to leave school at an early age to take on family responsibilities. Financial difficulties, emotional distress and limited opportunities gradually affected his well-being. In search of temporary relief, he began using drugs in the company of peers, eventually developing substance dependence.

This affected his health, work productivity and relationships with family members. Financial strain, social stigma and limited access to nearby rehabilitation services further compounded his difficulties. Despite these challenges, Rahul aspired to rebuild his life and fulfil his dream of establishing his own transportation business.

A turning point came when Rahul received support under the NAPDDR through the Drug De-addiction and Rehabilitation Centre (DDAC) operated by WODWICHEE in Karimganj, Assam. With guidance from doctors, counsellors and centre staff, he underwent residential rehabilitation and received medical treatment, individual and group counselling, family counselling, cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT), 12-Step Therapy, yoga and meditation.

These comprehensive services supported his recovery, helped him develop healthier habits and enabled him to regain confidence. Family counselling and community reintegration support further assisted him in rebuilding relationships and preparing for a more stable future.

With sustained support and determination, Rahul gradually regained control over his life and redirected his efforts towards productive work. Today, he operates his own small transportation business and earns more than he did previously. The improvement in his income has strengthened his financial stability and enabled him to contribute more effectively to his family’s well-being. His journey demonstrates how access to treatment, rehabilitation and continued support can help individuals overcome substance dependence and pursue their aspirations with renewed confidence.

The support provided to Rahul reflects the importance of comprehensive rehabilitation in addressing not only substance dependence but also the social and economic challenges associated with it. Through initiatives under NAPDDR, the Ministry seeks to strengthen access to de-addiction services, promote recovery and facilitate the social reintegration of individuals affected by substance use. Rahul’s experience underscores how appropriate care and sustained support can help individuals rebuild their lives, restore their livelihoods and move towards a more secure future.

The Ministry continues to encourage awareness, early intervention, access to treatment and community-based support to address substance dependence and promote a healthier, more inclusive society.

2328507.title: Legislative Department and Department of Legal Affairs Take Integrity Pledge to Mark Vigilance Awareness Week
2328507.body_html:
Ministry of Law and Justice
Legislative Department and Department of Legal Affairs Take Integrity Pledge to Mark Vigilance Awareness Week
Posted On: 26 OCT 2026 4:37PM by PIB Delhi

As part of the observance of Vigilance Awareness Week 2026, officers and officials of the Legislative Department and the Department of Legal Affairs, Ministry of Law and Justice, took the Integrity Pledge administered by Dr. Manoj Kumar, Additional Secretary, Legislative Department, at Hall No. 24000-B, Kartavya Bhawan-2, New Delhi, today.

The pledge reaffirmed the collective commitment of both departments to upholding the highest standards of honesty, integrity and ethical conduct in the discharge of official duties, while fostering a culture of transparency, accountability, fairness and good governance in public administration.

On the occasion, officers and officials reiterated their resolve to discharge their responsibilities with sincerity, impartiality and a strong sense of public service, while safeguarding the rights and interests of citizens and society at large.

The observance underscored the importance of vigilance, ethical conduct and individual accountability in preventing corruption, strengthening institutional integrity and sustaining public trust in government institutions.

The initiative reflects the Ministry of Law and Justice's continued commitment to integrity, probity and transparency in public administration, reinforcing the principle that ethical governance and public accountability are fundamental to effective and citizen-centric public service.

2328622.title: کوئلہ کی وزارت کےسی پی ایس یزنےخصوصی مہم 6 کے تحت اہم سنگ میل حاصل کیے،
2328622.body_html:
कोयला मंत्रालय
کوئلہ کی وزارت کےسی پی ایس یزنےخصوصی مہم 6 کے تحت اہم سنگ میل حاصل کیے،
130.16 لاکھ مربع فٹ رقبے کی صفائی کی اور بے کارسامان کی فروخت سے 53.94 کروڑ روپے کی آمدنی حاصل کی
प्रविष्टि तिथि: 26 OCT 2026 4:35PM by PIB Delhi

وزارتِ کوئلہ کے ماتحت مرکزی سرکاری شعبے کے ادارے (سی پی ایس ایز) خصوصی مہم 6 کے تحت صفائی ستھرائی کو ادارہ جاتی معمول بنانے اور الیکٹرانک کچرے کے بہتر انتظام کے لیے ملک گیر سطح پر بھرپور اقدامات کر رہے ہیں اور نمایاں نتائج حاصل کر رہے ہیں۔ اس مہم کے ذریعے دفاتر میں قیمتی جگہ خالی کرانے، کچرے کے مؤثر انتظام سے خاطر خواہ آمدنی حاصل کرنے اور دفتری ریکارڈ کو منظم بنانے میں کامیابی ملی ہے، جس سے صاف ستھرا اور زیادہ نتیجہ خیز دفتری ماحول فروغ پا رہا ہے۔

اس مہم پر عمل درآمد کا سلسلہ 31 اکتوبر تک جاری رہے گا۔ اس دوران سرکاری اداروں نے صفائی کے لیے ابتدائی طور پر نشان زد کیے گئے 1,565 مقامات کے ہدف کے مقابلے میں 1,696 مقامات کی کامیابی سے صفائی کی۔ اس طرح مجموعی طور پر 130.16 لاکھ مربع فٹ رقبے کو صاف کیا گیا، جو مقررہ ہدف 101.80 لاکھ مربع فٹ سے کہیں زیادہ ہے۔

دفاتر کے ماحول کو بہتر بنانے کے ساتھ ساتھ، اس مہم کے ذریعے کچرے کے مؤثر انتظام سے معاشی اور ماحولیاتی فوائد بھی حاصل ہوئے۔ مجموعی طور پر 16,158 میٹرک ٹن بے کارسامان اور کباڑ کو کامیابی سے ٹھکانے لگایا گیا، جو مقررہ ہدف 10,909 میٹرک ٹن سے زیادہ ہے۔ ناکارہ سامان کی اس بڑے پیمانے پر فروخت اور تلفی کے نتیجے میں سرکاری خزانے کو 53,94,62,602.45 روپے، یعنی تقریباً 53.94 کروڑ روپے کی آمدنی حاصل ہوئی۔

مزید برآں ریکارڈ کو منظم انداز میں محفوظ کرنے اور اسے ڈیجیٹل شکل دینے کی کوششوں کے ذریعے انتظامی کارکردگی میں نمایاں بہتری آئی ہے۔ حکام نے 59,593 فائلوں کے مقررہ ہدف کے مقابلے میں کاغذی اور برقی ریکارڈ پر مشتمل مجموعی طور پر 78,635 فائلوں کا جائزہ لیا، جبکہ ان میں سے 70,093 فائلوں کو غیر ضروری قرار دے کر ریکارڈ سے خارج کر دیا گیا اور بند کر دیا گیا۔ یہ اقدامات حکومتی امور اور دفتری طریقۂ کار کو مزید منظم اور مؤثر بنانے کی عکاسی کرتے ہیں۔

اداروں میں صفائی ستھرائی کو مستقل معمول بنانے اور پائیدار انتظامی طریقۂ کار کو فروغ دینے کے اپنے عزم کو عملی جامہ پہناتے ہوئے، وزارتِ کوئلہ کے ماتحت مرکزی سرکاری شعبے کے ادارے (سی پی ایس ایز) صفائی ستھرائی کی اختراعی مہمات اور جگہ کے مؤثر استعمال کی حکمتِ عملیوں کے ذریعے نئے معیارات قائم کر رہے ہیں۔ اس مہم کے دوران اختیار کیے گئے نمایاں بہترین طریقوں میں درج ذیل شامل ہیں:

  1. ایس ای سی ایل کے صدر دفتر میں دوبارہ قابلِ استعمال بنائے گئے بے کار سامان سے الیکٹرانک کچرا جمع کرنے کے لیے ایک مخصوص ڈبہ تیار کیا گیا ہے۔ اسے الیکٹرانک کچرے کو منظم انداز میں جمع کرنے اور الگ الگ کرنے کے لیے رکھا گیا ہے۔ یہ اقدام مہم کے اس مقصد سے ہم آہنگ ہے کہ الیکٹرانک کچرے کو مؤثر طریقے سے جمع کیا جائے، اس کی چھانٹی کی جائے اور اسے مناسب طریقے سے ٹھکانے لگایا جائے۔

 

 

  1. سی آئی ایل کے صدر دفتر کی کینٹین کی جدید کاری: تقریباً دس سال کے عرصے پر محیط جامع تزئین و آرائش کے بعد کینٹین کو نیا نام ‘سلینٹرو’دے کر 5 اکتوبر 2026 کو افتتاح کیا گیا۔ اس منصوبے کے تحت کینٹین کے بنیادی ڈھانچے اور ماحول کو بہتر بنایا گیا، تاکہ ملازمین کو کھانے پینے کے لیے صاف ستھرا، آرام دہ اور ان کی ضروریات کے مطابق سازگار ماحول فراہم کیا جا سکے۔

 

 

  1. ڈبلیو سی ایل کی جانب سے قبائلی طالبات کی تعلیمی معاونت: ویسٹرن کول فیلڈز لمیٹڈ (ڈبلیو سی ایل) نے ماتا شبری گرلز رہائشی تعلیمی مرکز، پراسیا، چھندواڑہ میں 160 سے زائد طالبات کو تعلیمی معاونت اور بنیادی سہولتیں فراہم کیں۔ ان طالبات کا تعلق زیادہ تر قبائلی برادریوں اور کان کنی والے علاقوں سے ہے۔ اس اقدام کا مقصد انہیں اعلیٰ تعلیم کے حصول میں مدد فراہم کرنا ہے۔

 

 

  1. ڈبلیو سی ایل کی جانب سے بچوں کے لیے ‘‘کچرے سے کمال’’ ورکشاپس: بچوں میں تخلیقی انداز سے ناکارہ اشیا کو دوبارہ قابلِ استعمال بنانے کی حوصلہ افزائی کے لیے دلچسپ اور عملی ورکشاپس منعقد کی گئیں۔ ان ورکشاپس کا مقصد کچرے کو کارآمد وسائل میں تبدیل کرنے کا شعور اجاگر کرنا اور کم عمری ہی سے بچوں میں ماحول کے تحفظ کی ذمہ داری کا احساس پیدا کرنا ہے۔

 

 

  1. کام کے مقام پر ماہواری کے دوران حفظانِ صحت کی سہولتوں کا فروغ: خواتین ملازمین اور کام کرنےوالی خواتین کو ماہواری کے دوران استعمال ہونے والے سینیٹری نیپکن بآسانی فراہم کرنے کے لیے سی آئی ایل کے صدر دفتر میں سینیٹری نیپکین فراہم کرنے والی مشینیں نصب کی گئی ہیں۔ اس اقدام کا مقصد خواتین کی ضروریات کا خیال رکھتے ہوئے کام کی جگہ پر ایک جامع، سازگار اور خواتین دوست ماحول کو فروغ دینا ہے۔

2328501.ministry: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
2328501.body_html:
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
Ministry of New & Renewable Energy Reviews Progress of Swachhata and File Disposal under Special Campaign 6.0
Posted On: 26 OCT 2026 4:32PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) undertook a review of cleanliness in its office sections and the status of file disposal under Special Campaign 6, aimed at institutionalising Swachhata and minimising pendency in government offices.

On 26th October 2026, Shri Aditya Pratap Singh, Director, MNRE, accompanied by Shri Rajat Yadav, Under Secretary, inspected various sections of the Ministry at Atal Akshaya Urja Bhawan, Lodhi Road, New Delhi.

During the inspection, the officers reviewed the maintenance and organisation of office spaces and emphasised the need to ensure cleanliness and proper utilisation of available space. The status of file disposal was also reviewed, with emphasis on the timely processing of files and expeditious clearance of pending cases.

The review reiterated the importance of regular monitoring, efficient file management and the active participation of officers and staff in achieving the objectives of Special Campaign 6. MNRE remains committed to promoting Swachhata, improving workplace organisation and reducing pendency through sustained efforts and effective administrative practices.

2328490.title: Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Observes Vigilance Awareness Week 2026 with Integrity Pledge
2328490.ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
2328490.body_html:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Observes Vigilance Awareness Week 2026 with Integrity Pledge
Union Health Minister Shri J. P. Nadda Leads Integrity Pledge Ceremony at the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Officers and officials of the Ministry reaffirm commitment to probity, transparency, accountability and a corruption-free public service
Posted On: 26 OCT 2026 4:22PM by PIB Delhi

Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW) observed Vigilance Awareness Week 2026 with an Integrity Pledge-taking ceremony Today at Kartavya Bhawan-1, New Delhi, reaffirming its commitment to probity, transparency, accountability and ethical conduct in public administration.

Union Minister of Health and Family Welfare, Shri J. P. Nadda, administered the Integrity Pledge in the Presence of Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare and AYUSH Ministry (Independent) Shri Prataprao Jadhav and Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, Smt. Anupriya Patel to senior officers of the Ministry. Other officers and officials of the Ministry participated in the ceremony virtually from their respective offices.

 

 

Vigilance Awareness Week is observed annually during the week in which the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, falling on 31 October, is commemorated. This year, the observance is being held from 26 October to 1 November 2026 on the theme “सत्यनिष्ठा से समृद्धि” (Probity for Prosperity). The theme underscores the significance of honesty, integrity and transparency as essential pillars of good governance and public trust in institutions.

In keeping with the theme, the Vigilance Division of the Department of Health and Family Welfare is undertaking various activities under the Vigilance Awareness Campaign 2026 to strengthen vigilance awareness and promote ethical conduct among officers and staff of the Ministry and its subordinate offices, institutes and organisations. These initiatives seek to reinforce institutional accountability and foster a work environment guided by transparency, responsibility and adherence to established norms.

The Integrity Pledge reaffirmed the commitment of officers and officials to uphold the rule of law, maintain the highest standards of probity and transparency in the discharge of their duties. It further emphasised the importance of acting in the public interest, demonstrating integrity through personal conduct, and reporting any instances of corruption to the appropriate authorities.

The pledge underscored the collective responsibility of the Government, citizens and the private sector in combating corruption. It called for sustained vigilance and adherence to the highest standards of honesty and integrity in all spheres of public life.

 

The observance reaffirmed the Ministry’s commitment to maintaining high standards of ethical conduct and accountability in the discharge of official responsibilities, in keeping with the principles of transparent, responsible and effective public administration.

2328486.title: DAC clears capital acquisition proposals worth Rs 2.12 lakh crore for defence forces
2328486.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
DAC clears capital acquisition proposals worth Rs 2.12 lakh crore for defence forces
Posted On: 26 OCT 2026 4:21PM by PIB Delhi

The Defence Acquisition Council (DAC), chaired by Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh on October  26, 2026, accorded Acceptance of Necessity (AoN) i.e. in-principle administrative to various capital acquisition proposals of the Defence Forces at an estimated cost of about Rs 2,12,000 crore. For the Indian Army, approval was accorded for the procurement of High Mobility Vehicles (HMV), Self-Propelled Tracked Gun System, Gun Shot Response System (GSRS), Light Multi Role Helicopters (LMRH), Very Short-Range Air Defence System (VSHORADS), Platform Based Counter Unmanned Aerial System (C-UAS), Unmanned Aerial System Brick Long Range, Surveillance UAV, Integrated Surveillance and Strike System and Long Range Kamikaze Drone System. 

The HMVs will enhance operational capabilities, logistic support and mobility in challenging terrains. The Self-Propelled Tracked Gun System will provide matching mobility and firepower to mechanised formations. The GSRS will serve as a force multiplier providing real-time situational awareness of the forces. The LMRH will be used by both the Indian Army and the Indian Air Force for Reconnaissance and Surveillance, Combat, Search and Rescue of troops, Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief etc. The VSHORADS will engage new generation small size aerial threats, while C-UAS will enhance survivability of Tanks in the modern battlefield. The Surveillance and Drone Systems will enhance the surveillance and targeting capabilities of the Indian Army.

For the Indian Navy, approval was given for the procurement of Active Offboard Decoy System (AODS) and other major Naval platforms. The AODS will enhance the credibility of anti-missiles defence, especially against modern anti-ship missiles of adversaries. The indigenously designed and constructed major Naval platforms will possess modern-day warfare capabilities and enhance the combat capability of the Navy.

For the Indian Air Force, approval was accorded for the procurement of Helicopters, Air Defence Systems, Weapons and Mobile X-Band Doppler Weather Radar System to enhance the air defence and war fighting capabilities. The procurement of Special Utility Helicopters will help the Indian Air Force to meet the important air transport requirements. The X-Band Doppler Weather Radar System will provide high-resolution, localised weather surveillance in forward areas.

Out of the total AoNs accorded, approximately 82% of the procurements will be made from the Indian Industry.

2328480.title: TRAI releases Recommendations on ‘Authorisation Framework for Application-based Linear Television Distribution (ALTD) Services’
2328480.body_html:
Ministry of Communications
TRAI releases Recommendations on ‘Authorisation Framework for Application-based Linear Television Distribution (ALTD) Services’
Posted On: 26 OCT 2026 4:13PM by PIB Delhi

The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has today released Recommendations on ‘Authorisation Framework for Application-based Linear Television Distribution (ALTD) Services’.

In view of the evolving broadcasting landscape, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (MIB) has sent a reference to TRAI, under Section 11(1)(a) of the TRAI Act 1997, on 15th December 2025, to examine and recommend a regulatory framework for Free Ad-Supported Streaming Television (FAST) Services ensuring parity, content accountability and consumer protection.

TRAI has examined such services and observed that several applications aggregate and distribute scheduled linear TV channels to consumers, either as pre-installed applications on TV sets and other devices; or as downloadable mobile/smart TV applications; or as web-based applications accessible through web browsers. Considering such wider scope of service provisioning through connected TVs, the services have been broadly referred to as ‘Application-based Linear Television Distribution (ALTD) Services’ including FAST Services.

Accordingly, the Authority on 6th April 2026, had issued a Consultation Paper titled ‘Formulation of a Regulatory Framework for Application-based Linear Television Distribution (ALTD) Services (Including Free Ad-Supported Streaming Television (FAST) Services)’ and solicited comments from stakeholders. In response, 207 comments and 11 counter-comments were received and uploaded on TRAI's website. As part of the consultation process, an Open House Discussion (OHD) was held on 10th June 2026, providing stakeholders an opportunity to present their views on the issues under consultation.

Based on the comments and counter-comments received from stakeholders, inputs gathered during the OHD, and its own analysis, the Authority has finalised its Recommendations on the ‘Authorisation Framework for Application-based Linear Television Distribution (ALTD) Services’. The recommendations seek to establish a light-touch and future-ready policy framework for Internet-based distribution of linear television channels, while promoting innovation, ease of doing business, consumer protection and regulatory certainty. These recommendations are built upon and complement the broader authorisation framework recommended by the Authority in its recommendations on ‘Framework for Service Authorisations for provision of Broadcasting Services under the Telecommunications Act, 2023’ issued on 21st February 2025.

Since ‘ALTD Service’ aggregates and distributes linear television channels over public Internet or other IP-based networks and provides consumers with a television viewing experience akin to conventional television distribution platforms across a variety of Internet-enabled devices, the Authority has recommended that ‘ALTD Service’ be introduced as a distinct sub-category under ‘Television Channel Distribution Services’ within the broadcasting authorisation framework under Section 3(1)(a) of the Telecommunications Act, 2023.  The recommendations further prescribe an authorisation framework, specifying the terms and conditions governing both the grant of authorisation and the provisioning of ‘ALTD Service’. The recommendations also provide obligations for key stakeholders like Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs), Operating System (OS) providers and the broadcasters/content owners of the TV channels; measures for consumer protection; and inclusion of ALTD viewership in the television audience measurement framework, thereby covering all aspects of a linear television distribution services.

The salient points of the Recommendations are given below:

  • Introduction of ‘ALTD Service’ under Section 3(1)(a) of the Telecommunications Act, 2023.
  • ‘ALTD Service’ is defined as aggregation of linear television channels that have been approved by the Central Government, including ‘Internet-native linear television channels’ (with approved name and logo), along with ALTD application provider’s own platform service channels, and its distribution to the users, with or without value-added services including on-demand audio-visual content, over public Internet or other IP-based networks through applications, websites or any other similar consumer interface, accessed through Internet-enabled devices.
  • Its scope covers development, deployment and management of such applications for users in India and excludes broadcaster-owned platforms distributing only their own channels or the channels of subsidiary/holding company; and live streams on social media intermediaries.
  • The terms and conditions governing ‘ALTD Service’ authorisation should be notified as Rules under Section 56 of the Telecommunications Act, 2023, and the authorisation, channel registration and reporting processes should be enabled through an online portal.
  • The Application Provider has been recommended as the primary entity responsible for obtaining authorisation for providing ‘ALTD Service’ and for complying with the applicable authorisation framework.
  • A light-touch authorisation framework has been recommended, with a national service area, an initial validity of 20 years renewable for successive periods of 10 years, an application processing fees of ₹10,000 and a one-time entry fee of ₹1 lakh, with no authorisation fee, bank guarantee or security deposit.
  • The detailed terms and conditions of grant of authorisation; and common and specific terms and conditions applicable to ‘ALTD Service’ have been recommended in alignment with TRAI's Recommendations on the authorisation framework for broadcasting services, with suitable modifications, to reflect the application-based and infrastructure-light nature of ‘ALTD Service’.
  • MIB should maintain a ‘Master ALTD app repository’. The OEMs (including television manufacturers) and the OS providers should ensure that only authorised ALTD applications are made available through their devices and application stores. They will be required to submit an annual compliance report to MIB in prescribed format.
  • In addition to existing permitted/authorised television channels, a framework has been recommended for simple registration of ‘Internet-native linear television channels’.
  • Authorised entity of ‘ALTD Service’ should distribute only the television channels holding valid permission/authorisation or registration from the Central Government.
  • The Application Provider should serve as the primary point of contact for consumer complaints and grievance redressal relating to ‘ALTD Service’.
  • Viewership of television channels distributed through ALTD applications should be integrated into the television audience measurement framework, and authorised ALTD application providers should be permitted to publish anonymised periodic viewership data in accordance with the TV Ratings Policy, 2026.

The recommendations aim to facilitate orderly growth of Internet-based linear television distribution services by providing an enabling authorisation framework.

The Recommendations have been placed on the TRAI's website (www.trai.gov.in). For any clarification/information, Dr. Deepali Sharma, Advisor (Broadcasting & Cable Services), TRAI, may be contacted at Telephone Number +91-11-20907774.

2328483.title: Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Reviews Progress of Special Campaign 6 and Preparedness for Kayakalp Activities
2328483.ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
2328483.body_html:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Reviews Progress of Special Campaign 6 and Preparedness for Kayakalp Activities
Union Health Secretary Chairs Review Meeting, Calls for Visible, Sustainable Improvements in Cleanliness Across Health Facilities
Health Ministry to Undertake Kayakalp Activities on 27 October, 2026 Under Special Campaign 6 to Strengthen Swachhata in Government Health Facilities
Posted On: 26 OCT 2026 4:10PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare reviewed the progress of the ongoing Special Campaign 6, aimed at institutionalising Swachhata and minimising pendency in government offices. The review meeting also assessed preparedness for the dedicated one-day Kayakalp Activities on Sanitation and Hygiene, scheduled for 27 October, 2026.

The review meeting, chaired by Union Health Secretary Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava, was held virtually from Kartavya Bhawan-1, New Delhi, today. Heads of institutions and organisations, including Central Government hospitals, Central Public Sector Undertakings (CPSUs), the Central Government Health Scheme (CGHS), and other offices and units under the Department of Health and Family Welfare, participated in the meeting.

During her interaction with the representatives of health institutions and facilities, Union Health Secretary emphasised that the campaign must go beyond symbolic activities to bring about perceptible improvements in sanitation, hygiene, space management and the overall upkeep of public healthcare facilities. She underscored that healthcare facilities are high-footfall areas where proper sanitation and cleanliness are essential for effective service delivery. Ensuring swachhata and hygiene, she stressed, is crucial to enhancing the quality of services and improving the overall experience of patients and visitors. She encouraged the institutions to participate wholeheartedly in the Kayakalp activities scheduled for 27 October, 2026 and ensure that the improvements undertaken are perceptible and verifiable, bringing about a distinctive change in the appearance of their premises and the experience of visitors.

Furthermore, she also noted that 100 per cent of identified cleanliness sites had been cleaned, nearly 100 per cent of public grievance appeals had been resolved, and approximately ₹50 lakhs in revenue had been generated through auction and clearance drives.

A key focus of the discussion was the effective implementation of the principles of Reduce, Reuse and Recycle, alongside sanitation and hygiene measures, pest control, biomedical waste management, e-waste disposal and improved maintenance of public spaces. Institutions were encouraged to undertake disposal of obsolete records and materials, including through e-auctions, to create usable space and generate revenue also, wherever feasible.

Further, participating institutions were encouraged to share examples of innovative practices undertaken as part of the campaign. These included repurposing discarded materials into functional items such as plant stands and storage racks, refurbishing condemned furniture, digitizing medical records to free up valuable space, developing green spaces through plantation drives, and undertaking deep-cleaning and horticultural initiatives to improve the overall environment of healthcare facilities. 

Other initiatives shared by several institutions during the meeting included the disposal of long-pending scrap through authorized auction platforms, which helped in generating revenue for the institutions and also creating additional usable space within their premises. Certain institutions also introduced digital grievance redressal platforms and QR code-enabled feedback mechanisms to expedite complaint resolution and reduce pendency.

Union Health Secretary emphasized that the campaign’s impact must be assessed through direct feedback from visitors and beneficiaries also. She concluded the meeting with a call to all health institutions to document their initiatives, share achievements through designated digital platforms, and ensure that the Special Campaign 6 creates a cleaner, accessible and welcoming environment for patients, pensioners, staff and visitors.

The review meeting was attended by representatives of 336 Central health institutions from across the country, including AIIMS Guwahati, AIIMS Rishikesh, AIIMS Bhubaneswar, NIMHANS Bengaluru, CDSCO Ahmedabad, Lady Hardinge Medical College, Safdarjung Hospital and RIMS Imphal, among others.

About Special Campaign 6 and Kayakalp activities:

Special Campaign 6 is being conducted from 02 to 31 October 2026, with a focus on institutionalizing cleanliness practices and reducing pendency in government offices. As part of the campaign, the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare will undertake Kayakalp activities focused on sanitation and hygiene on 27 October, 2026, as a dedicated one-day initiative to institutionalize swachhata in government offices.

2328468.title: INS TRISHUL ARRIVES AT CIVITAVECCHIA, ITALY
2328468.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
INS TRISHUL ARRIVES AT CIVITAVECCHIA, ITALY
Posted On: 26 OCT 2026 3:56PM by PIB Delhi

Indian Naval Ship Trishul arrived at Civitavecchia, Italy, on 25 Oct 2026, during her ongoing operational deployment to the Mediterranean Sea.

Prior to entering harbour, the ship undertook a Passage Exercise (PASSEX) with Italian Naval Ship Carlo Margottini. The exercise featured coordinated manoeuvring drills, communication procedures, replenishment approaches, cross-deck landings, personnel transfers and boarding operations. The PASSEX facilitated the exchange of Best Practices and enhanced operational synergy between the two Navies.

During the port call, professional interactions, cultural visits and exchanges are scheduled. The ship will also be open to visitors, providing an opportunity to engage with the Indian Navy’s maritime traditions and capabilities.

The port call underscores the enduring maritime partnership between India and Italy and reflects the commitment of both Navies to enhancing professional linkages and operational cooperation.

2328441.title: LOK SABHA SPEAKER INAUGURATES 12TH BRICS PARLIAMENTARY FORUM 2026; CALLS FOR EMPOWERING PARLIAMENTS TO ADVANCE PEOPLE-CENTRIC DEVELOPMENT
2328441.body_html:
Lok Sabha Secretariat
LOK SABHA SPEAKER INAUGURATES 12TH BRICS PARLIAMENTARY FORUM 2026; CALLS FOR EMPOWERING PARLIAMENTS TO ADVANCE PEOPLE-CENTRIC DEVELOPMENT
PRIME MINISTER SHRI NARENDRA MODI INTERACTS WITH PARLIAMENTARY DELEGATIONS FROM BRICS COUNTRIES
UNANIMOUS ADOPTION OF JOINT STATEMENT AT BRICS SUMMIT UNDER THE CHAIRMANSHIP OF PRIME MINISTER SHRI NARENDRA MODI WAS A LANDMARK ACHIEVEMENT: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
TRUE MEASURE OF BRICS SUCCESS LIES IN TRANSLATING DIALOGUE INTO TANGIBLE OUTCOMES: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
PARLIAMENTS CAN FOSTER MUTUAL TRUST, BRIDGE DIFFERENCES AND ADVANCE PEACEFUL RESOLUTION OF GLOBAL CHALLENGES: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
VOICE OF THE GLOBAL SOUTH MUST FIND EXPRESSION IN CONCRETE POLICIES AND MEANINGFUL COOPERATION: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
HARNESS THE ASPIRATIONS OF YOUTH AND CHANNEL THEIR TALENTS INTO NATION-BUILDING: LOK SABHA SPEAKER URGES BRICS PARLIAMENTS
DEVELOPMENT AND ENVIRONMENTAL STEWARDSHIP ARE INSEPARABLE; COLLECTIVE ACTION ESSENTIAL FOR A SUSTAINABLE AND INCLUSIVE WORLD: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
Posted On: 26 OCT 2026 3:24PM by PIB Delhi

Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla today inaugurated the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum 2026 at the historic Samvidhan Sadan in the Parliament House Complex, New Delhi, calling upon the Parliaments of BRICS member and partner countries to strengthen their collective resolve towards people-centric development, global peace, sustainability and international cooperation. Emphasizing the transformative potential of parliamentary engagement, he underscored the need to harness the collective wisdom of nations to address shared challenges, deepen mutual understanding and bring meaningful, positive change to the lives of citizens.

Welcoming the parliamentary delegations from BRICS member and partner countries to India, Shri Birla observed that their presence reflected a shared commitment to dialogue, parliamentary cooperation, mutual respect and democratic values. He noted that notwithstanding their geographical, cultural, linguistic and social diversity, the countries were united by their faith in democratic ideals and a common sense of responsibility towards humanity. The true strength of BRICS, he said, lay in its ability to transform diversity into a source of strength, shared purpose and collective progress.

Describing the unanimous adoption of the Joint Statement at the BRICS Summit of Heads of State and Government held in New Delhi under the chairmanship of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi as a significant milestone, Shri Birla expressed his appreciation to the member countries. He emphasized that the real challenge now lay in translating the commitments embodied in the Joint Statement into tangible and lasting outcomes. Parliaments, through their legislative functions, budgetary processes, deliberations and oversight, could play a pivotal role in ensuring that these commitments translated into meaningful action and delivered tangible benefits to citizens.

Observing that the world was passing through a period of profound uncertainty, Shri Birla highlighted the mounting challenges posed by regional conflicts, wars, economic instability, trade tensions, terrorism and climate change. Their consequences, he noted, transcended national boundaries and called for a spirit of collective responsibility. In such a challenging global landscape, dialogue, diplomacy and cooperation assumed even greater significance. Parliaments, as vibrant expressions of the people's will, could serve as bridges of understanding, strengthen mutual confidence, ease international tensions and help advance peaceful and constructive responses to global challenges. Through parliamentary diplomacy, elected representatives could exchange perspectives, draw upon shared experiences, identify common interests and open new avenues for meaningful international cooperation.

Shri Birla observed that BRICS carried the significant responsibility of amplifying the voice of the Global South and advancing its aspirations on the world stage. He emphasized that this aspiration must move beyond the realm of dialogue and declarations to find concrete expression in responsive policies, practical cooperation and collective initiatives that improve people's lives. The strength of the grouping, he noted, would be reflected in its ability to transform shared aspirations into purposeful action and ensure that the concerns and priorities of developing nations received due consideration in global decision-making.

Highlighting the theme of the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum 2026, ‘Strengthening Parliaments for People-Centric Development’, Shri Birla said it held particular relevance in the contemporary global context. The two-day Forum would provide an important platform for comprehensive deliberations on four interconnected pillars—resilience, innovation, cooperation and sustainability—each essential to strengthening democratic institutions and advancing inclusive development in an increasingly interconnected world.

Emphasizing the need for resilient parliamentary institutions, Shri Birla stated that BRICS countries must continually strengthen their legislative frameworks and institutional capacities to ensure continuity, accountability and effective democratic oversight, particularly in times of uncertainty and disruption. Parliaments, he observed, were living institutions that must evolve in step with the changing aspirations of the people. Their strength lay not merely in their constitutional authority but also in their ability to foster constructive dialogue, build consensus, uphold transparency and remain steadfastly accountable to the citizens they represent.

Underscoring the transformative role of innovation in parliamentary functioning, the Lok Sabha Speaker said that innovation extended beyond the adoption of new technologies to encompass fresh ideas, progressive practices and institutional reforms that made democratic institutions more effective, transparent, participatory and responsive. By embracing constructive change and strengthening institutional capabilities, parliaments could enhance the quality of deliberation, improve public engagement and respond more meaningfully to the evolving expectations of citizens.

Reflecting on the immense potential of parliamentary cooperation, Shri Birla observed that the diversity of BRICS countries was not a constraint but a valuable asset that could be harnessed for the common good. By sharing experiences, exchanging best practices and learning from one another's institutional strengths, their parliaments could collectively devise innovative responses to shared challenges. Such sustained engagement, he said, would help lay the foundations of a more equitable, inclusive and peaceful world.

He further emphasized that the essence of parliamentary diplomacy lay in fostering a culture of cooperation while fully respecting the sovereignty and distinctive perspectives of every nation. Differences in national circumstances need not impede the pursuit of common objectives; rather, constructive engagement could turn diverse viewpoints into opportunities for mutual learning and collective advancement. Calling for renewed commitment among BRICS member countries, Shri Birla urged them to transform experience into joint action, understanding into enduring trust, and dialogue into concrete and meaningful cooperation.

Turning to the imperative of sustainable development, Shri Birla observed that Indian philosophical thought regarded development and environmental preservation as complementary, mutually reinforcing pursuits. This holistic perspective, he said, offered an important guiding principle for the parliaments of BRICS countries. Development must not come at the cost of ecological balance; instead, policies for economic and social progress must be shaped by environmental responsibility, long-term sustainability and a deep commitment to safeguarding the interests of future generations. Collective action in this direction was indispensable to building a world that was prosperous, inclusive and environmentally secure.

Drawing attention to the hopes and aspirations of the younger generation, Shri Birla observed that today's youth were equipped with growing access to quality education and technological knowledge, alongside an immense desire to innovate, excel and contribute to society. Their aspirations must be met with meaningful opportunities, dignity and an enabling environment in which their talents could flourish. Parliaments, he emphasised, had a vital responsibility to listen to young voices, understand their hopes and concerns, and create pathways through which their energy, creativity and capabilities could be channelled into nation-building. Empowering young people, he said, was not merely an investment in their individual futures but a commitment to the collective destiny of nations.

Referring to Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's vision of transforming BRICS into an ‘ecosystem of solutions’, the Lok Sabha Speaker underscored that the true measure of the Forum's success would lie not in the breadth of its discussions alone, but in the depth of its outcomes and the difference they made to people's lives. He called upon the parliaments of member countries to work towards a forward-looking agenda for a shared future, ensuring that dialogue culminated in action and cooperation yielded measurable results.

Shri Birla observed that although BRICS countries differed in their national circumstances, developmental priorities and perspectives, they were united by fundamental aspirations: peace, security, mutual respect, equal opportunities and a better quality of life for their citizens. These shared aspirations, he said, provided a strong foundation for deeper engagement and purposeful cooperation. The BRICS Parliamentary Forum must therefore emerge as a dynamic platform for building confidence, fostering understanding and advancing collective action in pursuit of these common goals.

Expressing confidence in the outcomes of the deliberations, Shri Birla said that the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum would further deepen the bonds of partnership among member countries and contribute meaningfully to the emergence of a more inclusive, peaceful and sustainable world. He expressed the hope that the discussions would impart fresh impetus to mutual trust and international cooperation, strengthen the collective commitment to people-centric development, and reinforce the shared determination of BRICS countries to translate common aspirations into enduring achievements.

On the occasion, Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha Shri Harivansh also addressed the gathering. The Secretary-General of the Lok Sabha delivered the welcome address.

A commemorative group photograph with Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri @narendramodi ji and the Speakers of Parliaments and Parliamentary Delegations from BRICS Member & Partner Countries, at the inauguration of the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum 2026 in New Delhi today . #BRICSParliamentaryForum #BRICS2026

— Om Birla (@ombirlakota) October 26, 2026

Addressed the inaugural session of the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum 2026 at the historic Samvidhan Sadan in the Parliament House Complex. As BRICS marks two decades of its journey, it stands as a powerful testament to the potential of diverse nations to build consensus, strengthen mutual trust and advance shared global aspirations. Representing nearly half of the world’s population, BRICS offers an important platform for fostering democratic values and deepening parliamentary cooperation. Under the theme “Fostering Parliaments for People-Centric Development,” the Forum provides an opportunity to reaffirm the central role of Parliaments in strengthening democratic institutions and addressing the pressing challenges of our time. Our deliberations on Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability will explore pathways to make parliamentary institutions more effective, transparent, accountable and responsive to citizens. Empowering youth, aligning aspirations with opportunities, balancing development with environmental sustainability, and amplifying the voice of the Global South must remain at the heart of our collective endeavours. Confident that the Forum will deepen parliamentary partnerships, foster meaningful dialogue and advance our shared vision of a more just, inclusive, peaceful and sustainable world. #BRICS2026 #BRICSParliamentaryForum

2328437.title: VIGILANCE AWARENESS WEEK 2026
2328437.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
VIGILANCE AWARENESS WEEK 2026
Union MoSJE Secretary Shri Sudhansh Pant Leads Integrity Pledge Ceremony at the Ministry
Emphasizes Transparency, Accountability And Corruption-Free Administration For Effective Delivery Of Welfare Schemes
Posted On: 26 OCT 2026 3:15PM by PIB Delhi

Marking the commencement of Vigilance Awareness Week (VAW) 2026, being observed from October 26 to November 1, Union Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Sudhansh Pant, today administered the Integrity Pledge to senior officers and staff of the Ministry, at a ceremony held in the National Capital.

The ceremony reaffirmed the Ministry’s commitment to promoting transparency, probity, accountability and ethical conduct in public service, while strengthening collective efforts to eliminate corruption from the administrative system.

Addressing the officers, Shri Sudhansh Pant emphasised the need to ensure transparency and efficiency across all Bureaus, Divisions, autonomous bodies, corporations and allied departments under the Ministry.

He urged officers to work towards establishing a corruption-free administrative system and accord highest priority to the timely disposal of public interest matters relating to various schemes and programmes.

The Secretary highlighted that efficient and transparent administration is essential to ensuring that the benefits of government initiatives reach eligible beneficiaries without delay. He also encouraged officers to sustain existing best practices, develop new result-oriented approaches and continuously identify and address systemic gaps that may create opportunities for corruption.

During the ceremony, officers and staff reaffirmed their commitment to upholding integrity, following the rule of law and discharging their official responsibilities in the larger public interest.

As part of the week-long observance, the Ministry is organising various awareness activities, including quizzes and expert lectures, to sensitise employees to the importance of vigilance, accountability and ethical governance. These initiatives aim to strengthen awareness of responsible conduct and reinforce a culture of integrity across the organisation.

Pertinently, the Integrity Pledge calls upon every citizen to uphold the highest standards of honesty, neither give nor accept bribes, perform all duties in an honest and transparent manner, act in the public interest, lead by example through personal integrity and report incidents of corruption to the appropriate authorities.

Through the observance of Vigilance Awareness Week 2026, the Ministry reiterates its resolve to promote a transparent, accountable and citizen-centric administrative framework and strengthen public confidence in the effective implementation of its welfare schemes and programmes.

2328434.title: Cabinet Secretary chairs a meeting of National Crisis Management Committee (NCMC) to review preparedness for the impending cyclone in Bay of Bengal
2328434.body_html:
Cabinet Secretariat
Cabinet Secretary chairs a meeting of National Crisis Management Committee (NCMC) to review preparedness for the impending cyclone in Bay of Bengal
Posted On: 26 OCT 2026 3:10PM by PIB Delhi

Cabinet Secretary, Dr. T. V. Somanathan today chaired a meeting of the National Crisis Management Committee (NCMC) to review preparedness for the impending cyclone in the Bay of Bengal.

Director General, India Meteorological Department (IMD) briefed the Committee that the deep depression over East central and adjoining Southeast Bay of Bengal has moved nearly Westwards and intensified into cyclonic storm ‘ARNAB’ and lay centered at 0530 hrs IST of today over East central and adjoining West central Bay of Bengal about 590 km Northwest of Sri Vijaya Puram (Andaman Islands) 650 km East-Southeast of Vishakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh), 730 km East-Southeast of Kakinada (Andhra Pradesh), 830 km East of Machilipatnam (Andhra Pradesh) and 910 km East of Bapatla (Andhra Pradesh).

It is forecast to move west-northwestwards till 27th October and then northwestwards towards Andhra Pradesh coast. It is likely to cross Andhra Pradesh & Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam as a very severe cyclonic storm with the maximum sustained wind speed of 115-125 kmph gusting to 140 kmph by forenoon of 28th October, 2026. Thereafter it is likely to affect districts in  Telangana, Southern Odisha, South & Central Chhattisgarh apart from Eastern Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.

The Chief Secretaries/ Senior officials of Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Telangana, Chhattisgarh and the Union Territory of Puducherry apprised the Committee of the preparatory measures being undertaken by the State Governments/ local administration. It was informed that adequate shelters and evacuation arrangements have been made, and necessary NDRF and SDRF teams have been kept on standby. District Control Rooms have also been activated and they are monitoring the situation.

Fishermen have been advised not to venture into the Southwest and adjoining central Bay of Bengal, and along and off the coasts of Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Yanam (Puducherry) from 26th to 29th October. Those already at sea have returned.

Central Ministries/Departments attending the meeting informed the Committee that all Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) are in place, necessary guidelines have been issued, and precautionary measures are being taken to minimise damage due to the impact of the cyclonic storm.

National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) informed that they have deployed teams, with additional teams on standby. Rescue and relief teams of the Army, Navy, Air Force and Indian Coast Guard, along with their ships and aircrafts, have been kept ready. Indian Coast Guard has so far shepherded multiple ships/boats to jetties/shore, and the remaining ships have been alerted to return to the coast. The Union Home Secretary informed the Committee that the Ministry of Home Affairs, NDMA and IMD are continuously monitoring the situation and coordinating with the Ministries/Departments, State Governments and other agencies.

Reviewing the preparedness measures of the Central agencies and the State Governments, Cabinet Secretary stressed that the objective should be to ensure zero loss of life and minimise damage to property and infrastructure. In the event of any damage, essential services should be restored in the shortest possible time. Cabinet Secretary also directed that in addition to Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Telangana, Chhattisgarh and the Union Territory of Puducherry, since high rainfall was also expected in Eastern Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, they should be suitably alerted by MHA/IMD.

 The meeting was attended by the Union Home Secretary;  the Chief Secretaries/ Senior officials of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Chhattisgarh, Odisha  and the Union Territory of Puducherry;  Secretaries in the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, and Ministry of Power; Member and Head of Department and Secretary, NDMA; Chief of Integrated Defence Staff to the Chairman, Chiefs of Staff Committee (CISC); Director General, NDRF; Director General, IMD; Director General, Indian Coast Guard; Director General of Media and Communication, MHA; and senior officers of IMD and the Ministry of Home Affairs.

2328432.title: National Overseas Scholarship: Yukti’s (Name Changed) Journey from Barriers to Global Opportunities
2328432.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
National Overseas Scholarship: Yukti’s (Name Changed) Journey from Barriers to Global Opportunities
Posted On: 26 OCT 2026 3:07PM by PIB Delhi

For many aspiring students, access to quality higher education is a stepping stone towards a brighter future. However, for students from disadvantaged backgrounds, social discrimination and financial constraints can create significant barriers to academic and professional advancement. The journey of Ms. Yukti, a 26-year-old postgraduate belonging to the Scheduled Caste (SC) community, highlights how targeted government support can help transform educational aspirations into opportunities.

From an early age, Yukti faced caste-based discrimination and social exclusion. Her family also experienced persistent financial difficulties, as her father was the sole earning member and worked in a low-paying job. Despite his education, occupational barriers and social bias limited his career progression, leaving the family with limited resources. Yukti’s parents nevertheless prioritised her education and encouraged her to pursue her ambitions. With no financial safety net, she relied on government schools and public scholarships to continue her studies.

Yukti aspired to pursue advanced higher education and build a meaningful career connected with research and academic development. However, the substantial cost of postgraduate education abroad appeared to be a major obstacle. A significant turning point came when she received support under the National Overseas Scholarship (NOS) Scheme of the Government of India during 2023–2024. The scholarship covered her tuition fees and provided an annual maintenance allowance of £9,900, helping her access international education that would otherwise have been financially out of reach.

The scholarship substantially eased the financial burden on Yukti and her family and enabled her to focus on her studies and professional development. Although rising living costs abroad meant that managing expenses remained challenging, the assistance provided essential support throughout her educational journey. Selection for the scholarship also gave Yukti a significant boost in confidence, affirmed her academic potential and strengthened her belief that she belonged in a competitive international academic environment.

Through her overseas education, Yukti gained valuable international exposure and advanced academic knowledge that strengthened her professional prospects. She has since transitioned into the private sector in India, securing professional opportunities and moving towards greater economic independence. While no specific change in income has been reported, her educational achievements and entry into professional employment mark meaningful progress towards her aspirations.

Yukti’s journey demonstrates the role of the National Overseas Scholarship Scheme in promoting educational inclusion and enabling students from Scheduled Caste communities to pursue higher education abroad. By providing financial assistance for tuition and maintenance, the scheme helps deserving students overcome economic barriers, broaden their horizons and build pathways towards professional growth. Her experience reflects how government support, family encouragement and personal determination can combine to turn educational aspirations into tangible opportunities.

2328428.title: Medical Research Must Address Humanity’s Healthcare Challenges: Vice-President at Dr. NTR University’s Ruby Jubilee
2328428.body_html:
Vice President's Secretariat
Medical Research Must Address Humanity’s Healthcare Challenges: Vice-President at Dr. NTR University’s Ruby Jubilee
“Dr. NTR, a Legend of India, Was a Leader Who Thought Beyond Regional Boundaries”: Vice-President
Technology Must Serve Humanity; Compassion Remains at the Heart of Healthcare: Vice-President
Doctors Must Lead Society’s Fight Against Drug Abuse: Vice-President
Posted On: 26 OCT 2026 2:54PM by PIB Delhi

The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today called upon medical institutions to strengthen research, foster innovation and develop solutions to pressing healthcare challenges, while addressing the 40th (Ruby Jubilee) Anniversary Celebrations of Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences in Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh.

Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan addressed the Ruby Jubilee celebrations of Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences in Vijayawada today. He called upon medical institutions to strengthen research and innovation to address humanity’s healthcare challenges, emphasising that technology must serve humanity and compassion remain at the heart of healthcare.

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) October 26, 2026
Congratulating the University on completing four decades of service to medical education and healthcare, the Vice-President said that the institution embodies the vision of former Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister and legendary leader Dr. Nandamuri Taraka Rama Rao. He noted that Dr. NTR’s vision and public service extended beyond regional boundaries, reflecting a broader commitment to the welfare of the nation.
Highlighting the expansion of medical education under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Vice-President said that the number of medical colleges in India has more than doubled, from 387 before 2014 to 846 at present. MBBS seats have increased by 172 per cent, from around 51,000 to over 1.4 lakh, while postgraduate seats have risen by 177 per cent, from around 31,000 to over 86,000.
Emphasising that the next frontier must be research and innovation, the Vice-President urged talented students to dedicate themselves to addressing healthcare challenges facing humanity. He expressed hope that researchers from Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences would achieve global recognition, including the Nobel Prize, through their contributions to medical science.
Observing that Artificial Intelligence, digital health, telemedicine and advanced diagnostic technologies are transforming healthcare, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan encouraged the University to establish collaborations with leading universities to provide students and researchers greater exposure to advanced research and emerging technologies. He stressed that technological progress must be guided by scientific validation, patient safety, data privacy and ethical responsibility, adding that technology cannot replace the compassion and human connection central to the doctor-patient relationship.
The Vice-President also called upon doctors and healthcare professionals to play a proactive role in creating awareness against drug abuse. Describing the fight against drugs as a collective responsibility, he urged the medical fraternity to lead efforts to build a drug-free society.

As part of the programme, the Vice-President joined the gathering in taking a pledge to say no to drugs and promote a drug-free society.He also released a souvenir commemorating the University’s 40-year journey.
Shri S. Abdul Nazeer, Governor of Andhra Pradesh and Chancellor of the University; Shri Kolusu Parthasarathy, Minister for Housing, Information and Public Relations, Government of Andhra Pradesh; Dr. P. Chandrasekhar, Vice-Chancellor of the University; Dr. M. K. Ramesh, President of the Medical Assessment and Rating Board, National Medical Commission, and other dignitaries were present on the occasion.

Earlier on his arrival at Vijaywada airport, Vice President Shri C P Radhakrishnan was warmly received by Shri S. Abdul Nazeer, Governor of Andhra Pradesh and Shri Nara Lokesh, Cabinet Minister , Govt. of Andhra Pradesh and other dignitaries.

 

Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan arrived at Vijayawada Airport today, where he was warmly received by Shri S. Abdul Nazeer, Governor of Andhra Pradesh, Shri Nara Lokesh, Minister for Information Technology, Electronics and Communications, and Human Resources Development, and other dignitaries.

2328424.title: GeM Promotes ‘The AABHAR Collection’ to Showcase India’s Cultural Heritage and Support Local Artisans
2328424.body_html:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
GeM Promotes ‘The AABHAR Collection’ to Showcase India’s Cultural Heritage and Support Local Artisans
AABHAR Collection Features 294 Product Listings from 10 State and Central Handloom and Handicraft Emporiums
Posted On: 26 OCT 2026 2:42PM by PIB Delhi

The Government e-Marketplace (GeM) is promoting ‘The AABHAR Collection’, a dedicated digital storefront showcasing curated gift items and hampers that reflect India’s rich cultural heritage. The collection features products associated with the One District, One Product (ODOP) initiative and Geographical Indication (GI) tags, providing government buyers with convenient access to distinctive regional products while supporting artisans, weavers, rural entrepreneurs and women-led enterprises.

The collection features 294 product catalogue listings from 10 State and Central Handloom and Handicraft Emporiums. These include COTTAGE from Central Cottage Industries Emporium, KHADI INDIA from the Khadi and Village Industries Commission, Garvi Gurjari (Gujarat), Himcrafts (Himachal Pradesh), Jharcraft (Jharkhand), Cauvery (Karnataka), Mrignayani (Madhya Pradesh), Marhati (Maharashtra), Purbashree (North East) and Poompuhar (Tamil Nadu).

Seven additional government emporiums and organisations are at an advanced stage of completing the seller onboarding process, which will enable them to offer their curated products through the AABHAR Collection storefront. These include the Coffee Board, Manjusha and Biswa Bangla (West Bengal), Jammu & Kashmir Handloom & Handicrafts Marketing Corporation Ltd. (JKHHMC), Merakai (Nagaland), Utkalika (Odisha) and Panthoibi (Manipur). The proposed addition of their product catalogues is expected to further diversify the collection’s regional representation and product range.

The collection includes handicrafts, handlooms, artisanal foods, pantry products and personal care items. It offers government buyers gifting options for official ceremonies, conferences, State events, foreign delegations, employee recognition, retirement functions and festive occasions.

Speaking on the launch of the AABHAR Collection 2026 initiative, Chief Executive Officer, GeM, Shri Mihir Kumar, said, “The Aabhar Collection marks an important milestone in enhancing visibility of indigenous arts and crafts, showcasing the rich tapestry of Indian heritage and culture, and empowering underserved seller groups through the network of Central and State Handicraft and Handloom Emporiums.”

Explaining the rationale behind the launch of ‘The AABHAR Collection’ in July 2024 and the current campaign, Additional Chief Executive Officer, GeM, and In-charge of Social Inclusion, Shri Ajit B. Chavan, said, “The idea was to provide an effective market linkage to the country’s artisanal ecosystem by integrating them through this #VocalForLocal storefront on GeM with the country’s public procurement landscape.”

He added that the collection enables Ministries, Departments, public sector undertakings (PSUs) and other government buyers to meet their gifting requirements while supporting indigenous products and local livelihoods.

Government buyers can explore the collection at https://gem.gov.in/Aabhar and contribute to promoting India’s cultural heritage and local enterprises through the procurement of #VocalForLocal gift hampers.

2328416.title: CBSE is organising the 4th National Summit on ‘Facilitating School-to-Work Transition’ in New Delhi
2328416.body_html:
Ministry of Education
CBSE is organising the 4th National Summit on ‘Facilitating School-to-Work Transition’ in New Delhi
Secretary, DoSEL, Shri T. K. Anil Kumar, highlights the importance of linking school education with higher education, skilling and employment
Posted On: 26 OCT 2026 2:16PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE), in association with the Sahodaya School Complexes of Delhi/NCR, is organising the 4th National Summit on ‘Facilitating School-to-Work Transition’ on October 26–27, 2026 in New Delhi. Secretary, Department of School Education and Literacy (DoSEL), Shri T. K. Anil Kumar, and Chairman, CBSE, Dr. Mandeep Bhandari, were present on the occasion, along with other senior officials from the Ministry and CBSE.

Speaking at the Summit, Shri Anil Kumar, outlined four key priorities of the Summit, namely, technology, digital safety and skills; design, creativity and innovation; recognition of skills across education systems through the National Credit Framework; and career guidance with equitable pathways. He called for seamless transitioning from school education to higher education, skilling and employment, enabling learners to make informed choices to help them pursue lifelong growth, contribute to society and live with dignity.

The two-day Summit aims to strengthen the integration of skill education with mainstream schooling and facilitate a smoother transition for students from schools to the world of work. It brings together school leaders, educators, industry experts and policymakers to deliberate on emerging workforce requirements and innovative approaches to prepare students for future careers. The Summit is also providing networking opportunities for the participants to connect and build partnerships for guidance and support from each other.

The Summit underscores the importance of breaking down barriers among different streams of education and equipping students with the competencies required to navigate an evolving employment landscape, as envisioned in the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020.

Through interactive sessions and expert discussions, the Summit is enabling participants to explore innovative pedagogical practices, emerging assessment approaches, digital integration in education, and effective models for strengthening skill education.

As part of the Summit, educators from CBSE-affiliated schools are presenting case-based papers and posters highlighting success stories and best practices in skill education. The Summit will also impart participants with insights on emerging trends and transformative practices in school education, along with innovative and practical strategies to enhance teaching-learning processes.

2328402.title: Department of Commerce Extends RELIEF Initiative under Export Promotion Mission Until March 31, 2027
2328402.body_html:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
Department of Commerce Extends RELIEF Initiative under Export Promotion Mission Until March 31, 2027
RELIEF Component II Offers 95% Risk Coverage to Encourage ECGC Cover for Export Shipments
Posted On: 26 OCT 2026 1:50PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Commerce has extended the timelines under Component II of RELIEF (Resilience & Logistics Intervention for Export Facilitation), a time-bound intervention under the Export Promotion Mission (EPM), until March 31, 2027. The extension was notified vide Notification No. 37/2026-27 dated September 30, 2026, in view of continued geopolitical disruptions in West Asia and their impact on maritime logistics across the Gulf and adjoining regions.

Component II of the initiative aims to encourage exporters to obtain Export Credit Guarantee Corporation of India (ECGC) cover for upcoming shipments to specified regions by providing 95 per cent risk coverage. The benefit is available for Standalone Policies and Whole Turnover Policies obtained on or after March 16, 2026. Under this component, the premium payable by eligible exporters is protected against increases beyond pre-disruption levels during the eligible period. The covered cargo categories include Full Container Load (FCL), Less than Container Load (LCL) and refrigerated (reefer) containers, excluding energy shipments.

Exporters seeking coverage under the RELIEF initiative are required to submit claims and supporting documents through the ECGC customer portal at www.ecgcltd.in. Guidance on generating user IDs and passwords, completing exporter registration and submitting claims under the initiative is available through dedicated video tutorials on ECGC’s official YouTube channel, @ecgcltd7016.

Launched on March 19, 2026, RELIEF is a targeted intervention to support Indian exporters facing extraordinary freight cost escalation, higher insurance premia and war-related export risks arising from disruptions in the Gulf and the wider West Asian maritime corridor.

The extension of RELIEF underscores the Government’s commitment to strengthening export resilience, sustaining trade flows and supporting Indian exporters amid continuing geopolitical and maritime logistics uncertainties.

Posted On: 26 OCT 2026 8:05AM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today extended his greetings to everyone on the occasion of Maharishi Valmiki Jayanti.

The Prime Minister stated that Maharishi Valmiki’s noble thoughts have remained the fundamental elements of Indian culture and heritage, which will continue to nurture and enrich the nation across every era. He added that his invaluable messages for humanity will forever serve as a guiding light for the citizens of the country.

2328288.title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi boosts morale of artisans by highlighting achievements of the Khadi and Village Industries sector in his ‘Mann Ki Baat’ programme
2328288.body_html:
Ministry of Micro,Small & Medium Enterprises
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi boosts morale of artisans by highlighting achievements of the Khadi and Village Industries sector in his ‘Mann Ki Baat’ programme
KVIC Chairman Shri Manoj Goel expressed gratitude to Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on behalf of millions of artisans from the ‘Khadi family’
Prime Minister’s appeal has given a new identity to Khadi and reinforced peoples’ trust in indigenous (Swadeshi) products
Posted On: 25 OCT 2026 9:50PM by PIB Delhi

Shri Manoj Goel, Chairman, Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC), Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India—expressed his heartfelt gratitude to Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi. In the 139th episode of his ‘Mann Ki Baat’ programme, the Prime Minister highlighted the rising sales of Khadi and village industry products and urged citizens to prioritize products made by local artisans during the upcoming festive season. Shri Goel stated that this reassurance from the Prime Minister serves as a source of honour, motivation, and infused energy for the millions of artisans, weavers, crafts men and rural entrepreneurs across the country who are associated with the Khadi and Village Industries sector.

Shri Goel said that due to the continuous inspiration of Khadi and village industries by the Prime Minister, this sector has gone beyond its traditional identity and has become an important source of employment generation, women empowerment, strengthening of rural economy and building a self-reliant India. With the inspiration of the Prime Minister, Khadi today has become the cultural heritage of the country as well as the self-confidence of modern India. It has emerged as a symbol of the spirit of *Swadeshi* (indigenous) and economic empowerment.

Expressing his gratitude to the Prime Minister, KVIC Chairman Shri Manoj Goel said, "The mention of Khadi and Village Industries in today’s episode—which coincides with the completion of 12 years of 'Mann Ki Baat'—is a moment of immense pride for us. It was from this very platform, on October 3, 2014, that the Prime Minister gave a call to purchase Khadi, thereby bestowing a new identity upon it. Since then, he has consistently encouraged purchase of Khadi and *Swadeshi* products. By highlighting that sales exceeded Rs 28 crore in a single day on Gandhi Jayanti, he has significantly boosted the morale of millions of Khadi artisans, especially women. KVIC and all Khadi artisans across the country are deeply grateful to the Hon’ble Prime Minister. We pledge to further strengthen his vision of 'Vocal for Local' and 'Atmanirbhar Bharat' (Self-reliant India) through a focus on quality, innovation, and by engaging the younger generation." This episode was particularly significant as it marked the completion of 12 years of the 'Mann Ki Baat' program, which first began on October 3, 2014, on the occasion of Vijayadashami.

Shri Goel recalled that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has, on several occasions through 'Mann Ki Baat', discussed the achievements of Khadi and appealed to the citizens of the country to purchase Khadi products. Following the appeal made in the very first episode on October 3, 2014—coinciding with Gandhi Jayanti—to buy at least one Khadi product, a record volume of sales was registered at the KVIC’s flagship outlet the very next day, on October 4, 2014. Subsequently, following similar appeals made on September 26, 2021 (in the 81st episode), September 25, 2022, and September 24, 2023, the Khadi Bhawan located at Connaught Place witnessed significant record sales of Rs. 1.34 crore on 2nd October in 2022, followed by over Rs 1.52 crore on October 2, 2023. In the 126th episode aired on September 28, 2025, the Prime Minister urged citizens to purchase at least one Khadi product on October 2 and take pride in its indigenous origin. Subsequently, in the 139th episode aired on October 25, 2026, he highlighted that sales of Khadi and Village Industries products had exceeded Rs 28 crore in a single day—on Gandhi Jayanti—and appealed to the public to buy local products during the festive season.

KVIC Chairman Shri Manoj Goel opined that, as a result of the visionary thinking and policies of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Khadi and Village Industries sector has witnessed unprecedented growth. In the 2025-26 financial year, the turnover of this sector surpassed Rs 1.87 lakh crore, while providing employment to over 2.04 crore people. He assured that, in the near future, the sector would also reach its turnover target of Rs 2.51 lakh crore.

2328265.title: Sarbananda Sonowal to pitch India's Shipbuilding Opportunity to Korean Industry during Korea Visit
2328265.ministry: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
2328265.body_html:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
Sarbananda Sonowal to pitch India's Shipbuilding Opportunity to Korean Industry during Korea Visit
Sonowal’s Four-day trip aims to deepen India-South Korea maritime ties with sights on becoming a top-five shipbuilding nation by 2047
You can serve as living bridges between your networks in both countries: Sarbananda Sonowal to Indian shipbuilders in Korea
We are looking for partnership with Korea in shipbuilding, shipping, ports and maritime logistics: Sarbananda Sonowal
Posted On: 25 OCT 2026 8:27PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW), Sarbananda Sonowal began a four-day visit to South Korea from today, pitching India's maritime opportunity to Korean industry as the two countries work to expand shipbuilding cooperation and move India toward its goal of becoming one of the world's top five shipbuilding nations by 2047.

Sonowal opened the trip in Busan, which he called the hub of Korea's maritime industry, with an interaction with Indian professionals working in Korean shipbuilding. India's Ambassador to South Korea, Gourangalal Das, welcomed the gathering and introduced the community, which includes people from Samsung Heavy Industries, Hanwha Ocean, HD Hyundai, DNV and the Indian Register of Shipping.

"Your presence in Korea, at the heart of one of the world's most advanced shipbuilding ecosystems, is a matter of pride for India," Sonowal said.

He urged them to see the framework adopted by the two countries in April, during South Korean President Lee Jae Myung's state visit to India, as more than a government agreement. The framework, called VOYAGES, covers cooperation in shipbuilding, shipping and maritime logistics.

"I want you to see VOYAGES not merely as a government framework, but as a platform for your professional growth and for India's maritime future," Sonowal said.

India aims to become a globally competitive centre for shipbuilding, ship repair, maritime manufacturing and logistics under Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Maritime India Vision 2030 and Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047, Sonowal said. India's Cabinet approved a series of policy incentives for the sector in September 2025.

Sonowal said India will need many more shipbuilders, marine engineers, naval architects, designers, welders, project managers and technology specialists. He asked the professionals to bring their Korean experience home or to support Indian companies from Korea.

"You can serve as living bridges between your networks in both countries," Sonowal said. He also encouraged them to mentor young Indian professionals and to take part in the India Ship Technology Centre and in the shipbuilding skills partnership between India and the Korea International Cooperation Agency.

Sonowal sought practical suggestions from the community on three issues: how to improve shipyard productivity and project execution, how to build a globally competitive skilled workforce, and how Indian and Korean industries can deepen cooperation in technology, manufacturing and innovation.

"We are looking for partnership with Korea in shipbuilding, shipping, ports and maritime logistics," Sonowal said.

The schedule includes meetings with leaders of global shipbuilding industries, engaging with the maritime industry bodies and other maritime think tank & research institutions.

Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal will take part in a ministerial roundtable in Busan for World Maritime Day, with ministerial representation from major maritime nations of the world, along with the secretary-general of the International Maritime Organisation (IMO), are expected.
